records.excerpt: Title: StoneCo (NASDAQ:STNE): A Classic Growth at a Reasonable Price Stock According to GARP’s Strategy URL Source: http://www.chartmill.com/news/STNE/Chartmill-50882-StoneCo-NASDAQSTNE-A-Classic-Growth-at-a-Reasonable-Price-Stock-According-to-GARPs-Strategy Published Time: 2026-07-13T10:40:49+02:00 Markdown Content: Peter Lynch’s approach to the stock market is a classic blend of growth and value investing, often described as a strategy of buying growing companies at reasonable prices. The core idea is to find businesses with sustainable earnings growth—not the explosive, unproven kind—that also trade at a discount to their intrinsic value. This means focusing on solid fundamentals: consistent profitability, manageable debt, and a price tag that doesn’t already reflect years of future success. For long-term, buy-and-hold investors, the goal is to build a diversified portfolio of ten to thirty such stocks and let compounding do the rest, ignoring short-term market noise. A screen designed to implement these rules recently flagged STONECO LTD-A ([NASDAQ:STNE](https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/STNE/profile)) as a potential candidate, and a closer look shows why it fits the profile. ![Image 1: STONECO LTD-A stock chart](https://www.chartmill.com/images/artgen/2026-07-13T38400358085231-STNE-ss.jpg) ### How StoneCo Meets Lynch’s Core Criteria The Peter Lynch screen applies five specific, quantifiable filters to narrow down the universe of stocks. StoneCo passes each of them, often with room to spare. * **Earnings growth within the sweet spot (15%–30%):** Lynch believed that companies growing earnings too fast (over 30%) are unsustainable, while those under 15% lack momentum. StoneCo’s earnings per share (EPS) grew at an average of **24.39% per year** over the last five years, landing squarely in that desirable middle range. This signals a business that has expanded at a healthy, repeatable pace rather than burning hot on a temporary trend. * **PEG ratio below 1:** The PEG ratio adjusts the price-to-earnings multiple for the growth rate, giving a clearer picture of value. StoneCo’s PEG ratio stands at an extremely low **0.24**, far below the maximum threshold of 1.0. In practice, this means that for each unit of projected earnings growth, investors are paying a fraction of what the market typically demands. It’s a textbook sign of undervaluation relative to the company’s own growth trajectory. * **Debt-to-equity below 0.6:** Lynch was wary of companies loaded with debt, preferring those that finance their operations through equity. StoneCo’s debt-to-equity ratio of **0.57** just sneaks under the ceiling. While Lynch personally favored a stricter limit of 0.25, the current figure still indicates a capital structure that relies more on shareholder funds than on borrowing. * **Current ratio of 1.0 or above:** This liquidity metric ensures a company can cover its short-term liabilities with its short-term assets. StoneCo posts a current ratio of **1.33**, providing a comfortable cushion above the minimum. It shows the business isn’t stretched thin from a cash-flow perspective. * **Return on equity above 15%:** Profitability is a non-negotiable for Lynch. StoneCo’s ROE of **28.69%** is well above the 15% bar and ranks among the best in its peer group. This level of return suggests the company is adept at reinvesting its earnings to generate additional profits. ### Why These Metrics Matter for the Strategy Individually, each of these numbers points to a company that is both growing and financially sound. Taken together, they form a profile that aligns directly with Lynch’s philosophy. The moderate growth rate (24.39%) avoids the danger zone where rapid expansion often masks operational fragility or leads to a crash. The low PEG ratio (0.24) confirms that the market hasn’t yet priced in that growth, offering a margin of safety. The manageable debt, solid liquidity, and high ROE reflect a business that can keep funding its own expansion without relying on excessive leverage or struggling to meet obligations. For a long-term investor, this combination reduces the risk of unpleasant surprises while leaving significant upside potential. ### A High-Level Look at the Fundamentals StoneCo receives an overall fundamental rating of 6 out of 10, which is driven by a standout performance in profitability and valuation, with some offsetting concerns in financial health. On the profitability side, the company is a leader: its Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) of 29.42% outperforms over 95% of its industry peers, and its operating margin of 50.72% is as impressive. Gross margins are high and stable, and the company has consistently generated positive operating cash flow. In terms of valuation, StoneCo is remarkably cheap. Its trailing P/E ratio of 5.75 is far below both the industry average (23.56) and the S&P 500 average (27.01), while its forward P/E of 4.71 is even more attractive. Multiple valuation multiples—EV/EBITDA, price-to-free cash flow—rank it in the cheapest tier of its sector. Where StoneCo gets docked points is in financial health. The Altman-Z score of 1.40, while better than about two-thirds of peers, still sits in a zone that signals some financial stress risk. The debt-to-free-cash-flow ratio of 7.17 also raises questions, as it indicates the company would need over seven years of its free cash flow to retire all debt. The current ratio is adequate but not stellar. These factors mean that while the company is profitable and cheap, investors should keep a watchful eye on its balance sheet. For those who want to dig deeper into the full breakdown, including the specific ratios and peer comparisons, a [detailed fundamental analysis](https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/STNE/fundamental-analysis) is available. ### Finding More Candidates Like StoneCo StoneCo is just one example of a stock that passes the Peter Lynch screen. Investors looking to build a diversified portfolio of similarly attractive companies can run the same screen themselves. It applies filters for earnings growth between 15% and 30%, a PEG ratio under 1, a current ratio above 1, a debt-to-equity ratio below 0.6, and a ROE above 15%. The screen also includes a minimum daily trading volume of 100,000 shares to ensure liquidity, though long-term holders may choose to relax that filter to catch smaller, undiscovered names. records.excerpt: Title: Descartes Systems Group (NASDAQ:DSGX): An Affordable Growth Stock With a Solid Foundation URL Source: http://www.chartmill.com/news/DSGX/Chartmill-50897-Descartes-Systems-Group-NASDAQDSGX-An-Affordable-Growth-Stock-With-a-Solid-Foundation Published Time: 2026-07-13T13:30:34+02:00 Markdown Content: The affordable growth strategy is a straightforward concept: find companies that are expanding their earnings and revenue at an above-average clip, but without the sky-high valuations that often accompany high-growth stocks. The logic is that if you can buy a growing business at a reasonable price, you have a better chance of seeing your investment appreciate as the company’s earnings catch up to its stock price. We ran this screen using ChartMill’s fundamental analysis tools, and one of the names that surfaced was Descartes Systems Group ([NASDAQ:DSGX](https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/DSGX/profile)). ![Image 1: DESCARTES SYSTEMS GRP/THE stock chart](https://www.chartmill.com/images/artgen/2026-07-13T48600221176440-DSGX-ss.jpg) ### Strong and Consistent Growth For an affordable growth strategy to work, the growth part has to be real and durable. Descartes delivers on both fronts. The company has posted impressive earnings per share (EPS) growth of 20.48% over the past year, and that’s not a one-off. Looking back over several years, its EPS has compounded at an annual rate of 25.39%. Revenue growth has also been solid, coming in at 12.79% for the last year and averaging 15.89% annually over the longer term. What’s more, the forward-looking estimates are equally encouraging. Analysts expect EPS to grow by 21.02% per year going forward, with revenue growth of 10.77% annually. This combination of strong past performance and sustained future expectations is exactly the kind of profile that growth-oriented investors look for. More importantly, the growth rate is stable rather than decelerating sharply, which reduces the risk of a sudden valuation collapse. ### Valuation: Not Cheap, but Fair for the Growth This is where the “affordable” part of the strategy comes into focus. Descartes trades at a trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 36.03, which on its surface looks expensive. That’s higher than the S&P 500 average of roughly 27. However, a simple P/E ratio doesn’t tell the full story for a growth company. * **Industry context:** Within the Software industry, the average P/E is 31.39, so Descartes is slightly above its peers on a trailing basis. But its forward P/E drops to 21.94, which is actually below the industry average of 33.21. That narrowing gap suggests the market is expecting earnings to grow into the current price. * **PEG ratio:** The PEG ratio (P/E divided by the earnings growth rate) is the more telling metric here. Descartes has a low PEG ratio, which indicates that when you account for its expected growth, the stock actually looks reasonably valued. * **Other multiples:** On an enterprise value to EBITDA basis, 72% of its industry peers are more expensive. Similarly, its price-to-free-cash-flow ratio is cheaper than 69.45% of its peers. The takeaway is that while Descartes is not a deep value stock, its growth profile justifies its current multiple. For a strategy that aims to avoid overpaying, this is a solid middle ground. ### Profitability and Health as Supporting Pillars Growth and valuation are important, but they mean less if a company is poorly managed or carries excessive debt. An affordable growth stock should also have a healthy business foundation, and Descartes checks those boxes as well. * **Profitability:** The company earns a ChartMill Profitability Rating of 8 out of 10. Its profit margin of 23.35% and operating margin of 28.20% both rank among the best in its industry. Returns on assets, equity, and invested capital are all well above the majority of peers. High margins and strong returns on capital suggest that the business model is efficient and that management is allocating capital wisely. * **Financial health:** Descartes carries no debt, which is rare in the software sector where acquisitions and buybacks often leverage balance sheets. Its Altman-Z score of 14.08 signals negligible bankruptcy risk, and its current and quick ratios both sit at 2.05, indicating ample liquidity. A debt-free company with strong liquidity has a much wider margin of safety, especially if economic conditions worsen. The combination of high profitability and a fortress-like balance sheet means the company can continue investing in growth without the risk of financial distress. This directly supports the affordable growth thesis, because it removes the common pitfalls that can derail a growth story. ### An Overall Picture for Affordable Growth Investors Descartes Systems Group offers a rare mix: double-digit growth in both earnings and revenue, a valuation that is reasonable when adjusted for that growth, and a financial profile that is both highly profitable and virtually debt-free. The ChartMill fundamental report assigns it an overall fundamental rating of 7 out of 10, with particular strength in growth (8/10), profitability (8/10), and health (8/10). While its valuation rating sits at a neutral 5/10, the context of its growth and quality makes that a fair—rather than a warning—signal. The Decent Value screen is designed to address precisely that challenge: it filters for stocks with strong valuation scores while still maintaining decent profitability, solid financial health, and respectable growth. This approach helps investors avoid the so-called value traps—companies that look cheap on the surface but have deteriorating fundamentals. One stock that emerges from this screen is Micron Technology Inc ([NASDAQ:MU](https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/MU/profile)), a company that appears to offer a rare combination of strong underlying business quality and attractive valuation. ![Image 1: MICRON TECHNOLOGY INC stock chart](https://www.chartmill.com/images/artgen/2026-07-13T40200270567133-MU-ss.jpg) ## Valuation That Stands Out in a Pricey Industry At the heart of any value-based strategy is the assessment of whether a stock is reasonably priced relative to its earnings, cash flow, and growth prospects. Micron’s valuation metrics are striking, especially when compared to its peers in the Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment industry. The company scores a Chartmill Valuation rating of 9 out of 10, which places it among the most attractively valued stocks in the sector. Several specific figures support this assessment: * **Price/Earnings (P/E) ratio of 21.70**: While this might seem elevated on an absolute basis, it is actually cheaper than 90.52% of industry peers. For context, the average P/E within the industry stands at 77.93, making Micron look decisively inexpensive by comparison. * **Price/Forward Earnings ratio of just 6.14**: This forward-looking metric is even more attractive. It indicates that based on expected future earnings, Micron is cheaper than 99.14% of companies in its industry and also well below the S&P 500 average forward P/E of 21.49. * **Enterprise Value to EBITDA**: This multiple also confirms the picture, with Micron valued cheaper than nearly 90% of its industry counterparts. * **Price/Free Cash Flow**: Here too, over 82% of industry peers are more expensive than Micron. What truly bolsters the value case is the PEG ratio, which accounts for growth. A low PEG ratio suggests that the market has not yet fully priced in the company’s expected earnings expansion. Given that analysts forecast earnings per share to grow by 179.38% in the coming years, the current valuation looks conservative—a classic scenario value investors look for. ## Profitability Metrics That Rival the Best A low valuation means little if the company cannot generate solid returns. This is where Micron shines. It achieves a Chartmill Profitability rating of 8 out of 10, driven by industry-leading margins and capital efficiency. Key profitability highlights include: * **Return on Assets (ROA) of 37.63%**: This outperforms 98.28% of industry peers, indicating how effectively the company uses its asset base. * **Return on Equity (ROE) of 50.11%**: A figure that puts Micron ahead of nearly 95% of its competitors, reflecting strong shareholder value creation. * **Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) of 39.30%**: This is better than 97.41% of peers and, critically, sits well above the company’s weighted average cost of capital (WACC), meaning Micron is genuinely creating value rather than just covering its cost of financing. * **Profit Margin of 55.91%**: This figure places Micron among the top 4% of its industry, and both the profit and operating margins have been improving over recent years. For value investors, strong profitability like this provides an important layer of safety. It suggests that the company’s cheap valuation is not a symptom of operational weakness—quite the opposite. ## Growth That Accelerates Rather Than Slows The third pillar of the Decent Value screen is growth, and here Micron delivers a score of 9 out of 10. The numbers are particularly impressive given the cyclical nature of the memory and storage industry. Recent and projected growth figures include: * **EPS growth of 600.62% over the past year**, reflecting a sharp cyclical recovery and strong demand for memory chips driven by artificial intelligence and data center investments. * **Revenue growth of 166.98% over the same period**. * **Longer-term average EPS growth of 23.98% per year**, which demonstrates that the recent surge builds on a solid foundation. * **Expected future EPS growth of 43.05% annually**, with revenue forecast to grow 45.25% per year. Importantly, the data shows that growth is accelerating: the EPS and revenue growth rates projected for the coming years are higher than those achieved in the recent past. This is a dynamic that value investors prize because it suggests the company’s intrinsic value is rising faster than its market price, potentially widening the margin of safety. ## Financial Health: A Solid Buffer While growth and valuation get the headlines, financial health provides the bedrock. The company earns a Chartmill Health rating of 7 out of 10, supported by strong solvency and liquidity metrics. Notable indicators include: * **Altman Z-Score of 23.39**: This is far above the danger zone and indicates virtually no bankruptcy risk. It also beats 79.31% of industry peers. * **Debt to Free Cash Flow ratio of 0.22**: At this pace, Micron could theoretically pay off all its debt in under three months. * **Debt to Equity ratio of just 0.05**: The company uses very little leverage. * **Current Ratio of 3.42** and **Quick Ratio of 2.98**: Both signal ample liquidity to cover short-term obligations. For value investors, a strong balance sheet reduces the risk that a temporary downturn or industry cyclicality could force the company into distress. It provides the staying power needed to wait for the market to eventually recognize the stock’s true worth. ## Putting It All Together Micron Technology Inc offers a profile that is rare in the current market: a company that is growing rapidly, highly profitable, financially sound, and yet priced at a significant discount to both its industry and its own growth trajectory. records.excerpt: Title: Slide Insurance Holdings (NASDAQ:SLDE): A Top Affordable Growth Stock Balancing Strong Earnings and Reasonable Valuation URL Source: http://www.chartmill.com/news/SLDE/Chartmill-50887-Slide-Insurance-Holdings-NASDAQSLDE-A-Top-Affordable-Growth-Stock-Balancing-Strong-Earnings-and-Reasonable-Valuation Published Time: 2026-07-13T11:40:36+02:00 Markdown Content: The affordable growth strategy aims to identify companies that balance two often conflicting traits: expanding earnings and revenue at an above-average pace, while still trading at a reasonable valuation. The idea is to avoid the extremes – not overpaying for a high-growth story that might falter, but also not settling for a cheap stock that has no momentum. This approach typically screens for solid growth rates, a price that isn't stretched relative to earnings, and a fundamental foundation of decent profitability and financial health. ![Image 1: SLIDE INSURANCE HOLDINGS INC stock chart](https://www.chartmill.com/images/artgen/2026-07-13T42000186726346-SLDE-ss.jpg) A current example passing through such a screen is Slide Insurance Holdings, Inc. ([NASDAQ:SLDE](https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/SLDE/profile)). A newly public company focused on residential homeowners insurance in coastal markets like Florida and South Carolina, SLDE presents a convincing case for why this strategy can find interesting opportunities. At first glance, the fundamental metrics suggest a company that has been executing well, and the market, for now, seems to be pricing it at a level that doesn't fully reflect that performance. ### Growth That Commands Attention The growth component is arguably the most critical pillar for an affordable growth stock, and SLDE scores exceptionally well here, earning a ChartMill Growth Rating of 8 out of 10. The numbers tell a clear story: * **Earnings Per Share (EPS) Growth:** The company has delivered explosive EPS growth of **108.98%** in the last year alone. Over a longer multi-year period, the average annual EPS growth stands at an even more impressive **166.13%**. * **Revenue Growth:** This isn't just a story of financial engineering. Top-line revenue has expanded by **36.50%** in the past year, with an average annual revenue growth rate of **68.31%** over the preceding years. This combination of triple-digit earnings growth and strong revenue expansion is a meaningful signal. It indicates the company is not only winning business but doing so with increasing efficiency and profitability. ### A Valuation That Makes Sense High growth often commands a high price, but that's where the "affordable" part of the strategy comes into play. SLDE's valuation metrics are notably undemanding, earning a ChartMill Valuation Rating of **8 out of 10**. * **Price-to-Earnings (P/E) Ratio:** The trailing P/E of **5.90** is a fraction of the S&P 500's average of **27.01**. This suggests the market is pricing in significant pessimism or is simply not yet recognizing the company’s earnings power. * **Forward P/E:** The forward P/E also sits at **5.90**, indicating that the expected earnings growth is not leading analysts to project a dramatically higher share price in the near term. * **Price to EBITDA and Free Cash Flow:** The valuation is further supported by other multiples. SLDE is cheaper than over **91%** of its industry peers based on EV/EBITDA and cheaper than over **86%** based on Price/Free Cash Flow. The presence of a low **PEG ratio** is key here. This metric divides the P/E ratio by the earnings growth rate, providing a clearer picture of value relative to growth. A low PEG ratio suggests that an investor is paying little for each unit of future earnings growth, which is the precise sweet spot the affordable growth strategy seeks. ### Profitability and Health as a Foundation Strong growth and low valuation are attractive, but they are only durable if the underlying business is profitable and financially sound. While SLDE’s ChartMill Health Rating of **5 out of 10** suggests some caution areas—specifically a lack of data on liquidity ratios from our report—the solvency picture is very strong. * **Minimal Debt:** The company carries very little leverage. Its Debt/Equity ratio is a mere **0.03**, and its Debt to Free Cash Flow ratio is just **0.03**. This means SLDE could theoretically pay off all its debt in a few weeks using free cash flow alone, a testament to its strong balance sheet. * **Increasing Value Creation:** The report also notes that SLDE’s Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) of **18.11%** is well above its cost of capital (WACC), confirming the company is creating value from its operations. Furthermore, it has been reducing its share count and improving its debt-to-assets ratio year-over-year. On the profitability side, the company’s ChartMill Profitability Rating of **7 out of 10** ranks among the best in its industry. Key metrics are outstanding: * **Operating Margin:** At **51.80%**, the company outperforms **100%** of its industry peers and has been improving over time. * **Return on Equity (ROE):** A stellar **44.09%** places it ahead of **99.31%** of its competitors in the Insurance sector. * **Return on Assets (ROA):** At **17.03%**, it remains above the vast majority of its peers. These numbers indicate a business that is highly efficient at converting its premium revenue into profit. Strong profitability provides a buffer for the company during challenging insurance cycles and supports continued investment in growth. For a more detailed breakdown of these individual metrics and scores, the full [fundamental analysis report for SLDE](https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/SLDE/fundamental-analysis) provides a thorough view of its financial standing. ### Why It Fits the Strategy Slide Insurance Holdings fits the affordable growth profile because it presents a rare combination. It has demonstrated a history of explosive growth, yet trades at a valuation that appears to offer a significant margin of safety. The high profitability and low debt levels provide a sturdy foundation, reducing the risk often associated with rapid expansion. While the slowing pace of future growth relative to its past trajectory is a point to monitor, the current price appears to already discount this potential deceleration, making it a textbook candidate for a strategy that seeks growth without paying a premium. If you are looking for similar opportunities that balance these crucial criteria, you can explore more results from the [Affordable Growth screen](https://www.chartmill.com/stock/stock-screener?sid=203&f=v1_50b500,p_pg20,sl_gr_7_X,sl_val_5_X,sl_he_5_X,sl_pr_5_X&s=val&v=14) to see what other stocks meet these standards. _Disclaimer: This article is for informational purposes only and does not constitute investment advice. By combining a technical filter, the Trend Template, with a fundamental check for high-growth momentum, this screen aims to identify companies that might be poised for further institutional demand. The idea is not to guess which stock will turn around, but to find those that are already showing clear leadership qualities, both on the chart and in their financial results. ![Image 1: INVESTAR HOLDING CORP stock chart](https://www.chartmill.com/images/artgen/2026-07-13T49200436845611-ISTR-ss.jpg) ## Meeting the Trend Template Criteria Investar Holding Corp ([NASDAQ:ISTR](https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/ISTR/profile)) passes the core technical hurdles of the Minervini Trend Template, which is designed to confirm a stock is in a healthy, long-term uptrend rather than just bouncing from a low. The following conditions are currently in place: * **Price Above Key Moving Averages:** The current price of $29.55 is above its 50-day SMA ($28.81), 150-day SMA ($28.14), and 200-day SMA ($26.98). This indicates the stock is trading above key short, medium, and long-term trend lines. * **Moving Average Alignment:** The 50-day SMA is above the 150-day and 200-day SMAs, and the 150-day SMA is above the 200-day SMA. This "stacked" alignment is a classic sign of a strong, sustained uptrend where shorter-term momentum is outpacing longer-term price action. * **Moving Average Trend:** Both the 50-day SMA and the 200-day SMA are currently rising, confirming that the underlying trend is still positive and not just a short-term fluctuation. * **52-Week Range Position:** The stock is trading at $29.55, which is roughly 41% above its 52-week low of $20.99 and approximately 7% below its 52-week high of $31.77. This satisfies the Trend Template's requirement of being at least 30% above the low and within 25% of the high, a condition that forces the screen to focus on strength and leadership rather than value traps. * **Relative Strength:** The Relative Strength rating of 77.32 indicates ISTR is outperforming 77% of all stocks in the market. While Minervini prefers scores in the 80s or 90s for top-tier setups, this still qualifies as a strong performer and confirms the stock is in demand. ## Why the High-Growth Fundamentals Matter for the Strategy The Minervini strategy is not just about price action; it insists on a fundamental catalyst. The screen complements the Trend Template by filtering for a High Growth Momentum rating of at least 4, ensuring that the technical strength is supported by real business growth. For ISTR, the fundamental picture shows notable acceleration that fits this profile perfectly. * **Significant Earnings Acceleration:** The most recent quarter's EPS growth (Q2Q) came in at a sharp 35.9%. This is a massive acceleration from the previous quarter, which saw a decline of -10.8%, and a clear improvement over the 20% growth from two quarters ago. This "acceleration" is exactly what the strategy seeks—a departure from recent trends that signals a new phase of expansion. * **Strong Revenue Surge:** The company reported an impressive 75% year-over-year revenue growth in its last quarter. This is a dramatic acceleration from a more modest 19% two quarters ago and a scant 3.7% in the prior quarter. A massive revenue beat often signals a strong catalyst, such as new business wins or expansion, which is a core element of the Minervini SEPA system. * **Improving Profit Margins:** The profit margin has been steadily climbing over the last four quarters, rising from 20.2% to a strong 32.3% in the latest period. This indicates the company is not just growing revenue, but managing its costs and gaining operational leverage, a sign of high-quality growth. * **Consistent Earnings Beats:** ISTR has beaten analyst earnings estimates in all of the last four quarters, with an average beat of nearly 18%. This consistency builds confidence among institutional investors, a key driver of the explosive price moves Minervini tries to capture. Taken together, the strong Trend Template structure and the accelerating fundamentals suggest that ISTR is a company that is currently executing well in a supportive technical environment. This is the core of the bottom-up approach: good companies making good things happen can often lead to good stock performance. ## A High-Level Look at the Technical Report The [full technical analysis](https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/ISTR/technical-analysis) on ISTR highlights a stock with a moderate long-term trend but a very compelling setup. The goal is to identify companies that can compound value over many years, driven by pricing power, efficient capital allocation, and expanding profitability. ![Image 1: BALCHEM CORP stock chart](https://www.chartmill.com/images/artgen/2026-07-13T39600468880601-BCPC-ss.jpg) **BALCHEM CORP ([NASDAQ:BCPC](https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/BCPC/profile))** is a specialty ingredients company serving the human nutrition, animal nutrition, and specialty products markets. It is a strong candidate for quality investors because it clears several demanding quantitative hurdles that separate high-performing businesses from the rest. One of the most critical metrics for quality is Return on Invested Capital (ROIC), and BCPC’s variant that adjusts for cash, goodwill, and intangibles stands at an impressive **33.13%**—more than double the 15% threshold typically required in quality screens. This indicates the company is highly efficient at turning its invested capital into profit, a hallmark of a business with a real competitive edge. Beyond profitability, BCPC shows excellent financial discipline and growth quality. Its **Debt/Free Cash Flow** ratio is just **0.97**, meaning it could theoretically pay off all its debt in under a year using its free cash flow. This is well below the maximum acceptable ratio of five, signaling that leverage is not a risk to the company’s long-term stability. Furthermore, its **EBIT growth over the last five years is 13.10%**, which outpaces its revenue growth, a clear sign that the company is achieving higher profitability through economies of scale or pricing power. The **Profit Quality** score, which measures how effectively net income is turned into free cash flow, sits at **114.37%**, showing that the company is not only profitable but actually generating more cash than its accounting net income suggests. A deeper look at the **[fundamental analysis report](https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/BCPC/fundamental-analysis)** for BCPC reinforces its quality credentials. The stock earns an overall score of **7 out of 10**, driven by outstanding marks in profitability and financial health. It scores a 9/10 in profitability, with industry-leading margins and returns—its profit margin of 14.95% and operating margin of 20.23% are both well above the industry median. The health rating sits at 8/10, with an Altman-Z score of 9.82, which places it in the safest tier for bankruptcy risk, and a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.13. While the valuation score is lower (2/10), reflecting a price/earnings ratio near 31, this is often the trade-off for quality: strong businesses command a premium, and the high profitability can justify the multiple over a long holding period. For investors looking to build a portfolio centered on enduring, high-quality businesses, BCPC checks all the right boxes: exceptional capital efficiency, low debt, and superior cash flow generation. records.excerpt: Nasdaq staff notified Apollomics on July 8 that its market value of listed securities met the $35M Rule 5550(b)(2) minimum for 10 straight days, closing the matter. FOSTER CITY, Calif., July 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Apollomics Inc. (Nasdaq: APLM ) (“Apollomics” or the “Company”), a late-stage clinical biopharmaceutical company developing multiple oncology drug candidates to address difficult-to-treat and treatment-resistant cancers, today announced that on July 8, 2026, it received written notice from the Nasdaq Listing Qualifications Staff (Staff) stating that the Company regained compliance with the Market Value of Listed Securities (MVLS) requirement, as set forth in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(b)(2) (Rule) for continued listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market, and the matter is now closed. As previously reported, the Company was notified by the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC on June 18, 2026, that it was not in compliance with the Rule because it failed to maintain a minimum MVLS of $35 million over the previous 30 consecutive business days. Since then, Staff has determined that for the last 10 consecutive business days, from June 23, 2026 to July 7, 2026, the Company’s market value of listed securities has been $35 million or greater. Accordingly, the Company has regained compliance with the Rule, and this matter is now closed. About Apollomics Inc. Apollomics Inc. is an innovative clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery and development of oncology therapies with the potential to be combined with other treatment options to harness the immune system and target specific molecular pathways to inhibit cancer. Apollomics’ lead program is vebreltinib (APL-101), a potent, selective c-Met inhibitor for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer and other advanced tumors with c-Met alterations, which is currently in a Phase 2 multicohort clinical trial in the United States and other countries. records.title: SK hynix's blockbuster Nasdaq debut fails to lift Seoul-listed shares
records.excerpt: SK hynix shares fell sharply in Seoul after the chipmaker’s blockbuster Nasdaq debut, as foreign and institutional investors sold while retail traders turned to its U.S.-listed ADR. Earnings miss concerns and ADR premium uncertainty added to the pressure. SK hynix's blockbuster Nasdaq debut fails to lift Seoul-listed shares Despite posting the second-largest U.S. listing on record, investors headed for the exits in Korea as a second quarter estimate projected the chipmaker to miss the market consensus. JIN MIN-JI JIN MIN-JI Published July 13, 2026 - 6:07 p.m. Modified July 13, 2026 - 6:16 p.m. An electronic display board at Hana Bank's trading room in central Seoul shows Korea's financial market on July 13. SK hynix closed down 15.37 percent on the day despite its successful Wall Street debut on Friday. NEWS1 SK hynix's blockbuster Nasdaq debut sparked a rush for the exits in Seoul, defying expectations that the landmark U.S. listing would lift its domestic shares. Foreign and institutional investors offloaded the stock, while retail investors — the backbone of the latest rally — are increasingly shifting their attention to the chipmaker's U.S.-listed shares. The debut failed to lift its Seoul-listed shares, as investors locked in profits amid uncertainty over the hefty premium on its American depositary receipt (ADR). An analyst report forecasting that the chipmaker’s second quarter earnings would miss consensus estimates added to the selling pressure. Despite its splash on the Nasdaq on Friday — the second-largest U.S. listing on record after Elon Musk’s SpaceX — SK hynix shares closed down 15.37 percent at 1.85 million won ($1,230) in Seoul on Monday. The selloff was largely led by foreign and institutional investors, who offloaded 1.41 trillion won and 1.47 trillion won, respectively, according to the Korea Exchange. GoogleAdmanager-KJD The sharp decline stood in stark contrast to the ADR's 13 percent surge in its Wall Street debut on Friday, where it closed at $168, implying a substantial premium over the Seoul-listed shares, with each ADR representing one-tenth of a common share. The sell-off also ran counter to expectations that the Seoul-listed shares would be rerated as the Nasdaq listing improves access for foreign investors. Related Article Black Monday: Kospi plunges 8.95%, closes below 7,000 Kospi circuit breaker triggered as index falls below 7,000 SK chief dismisses peak fears, pledges massive AI push after Nasdaq debut "It's common on the first trading day for investors to rotate out of the Korea-listed shares and into the U.S.-listed ADR, making the selloff largely a flow-driven move," said Hwang San-hae, a market analyst at LS Securities. “Because the market is still discovering the appropriate premium, volatility could increase in the early stages.” A pessimistic outlook for the chip giant also spread negative sentiment. SK hynix is projected to fall 8 percent short of its second quarter operating profit consensus, according to a report from Korea Investment & Securities on Monday. The brokerage forecast the chipmaker to log 60.4 trillion won in profit in the April-to-June period, falling short of the 65 trillion won consensus estimate. It attributed the shortfall to SK hynix’s heavier reliance on high bandwidth memory (HBM), which is expected to result in slower average selling price growth. Executives of the semiconductor and memory chip company SK hynix attend the company's opening bell ceremony at the Nasdaq market on the day of its initial public offering in New York on July 10. REUTERS/YONHAP "Starting in the third quarter, when HBM4 enters full-scale mass production and shipments, we expect average selling prices [ASP] to increase at roughly the market average," said Choi Min-sook, an analyst at Korea Investment & Securities. "We estimate that dynamic random-access memory and NAND ASPs in the second quarter rose by about 30 percent and 50 percent, respectively, from the previous quarter." The brokerage further cut the chip giant’s 2026 and 2027 operating profit estimates by 9 percent and 11 percent, respectively, not because of weaker earnings prospects but to reflect more realistic pricing assumptions based on long-term supply agreements that have already been signed. Amid the concerns, retail investors who have been the main drivers of the Kospi rally are rethinking their exposure to Korea. Investor deposits, a gauge of cash waiting on the sidelines to enter the stock market, fell to 107 trillion won as of July 9, roughly down 30 trillion won from the end of last month. “The anticipation of flow-driven catalysts, including the ADR listing and leveraged exchange-traded funds, had helped Korean semiconductor stocks decouple from the lackluster performance of their U.S. counterparts since May,” LS Securities' Hwang said. “Now that those expectations are fading, the sector is beginning to trade more in sync with the U.S. market." Despite the major sell-off, some analysts remain optimistic. Semiconductor and memory chip company SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-Jung attends the company's opening bell ceremony at the Nasdaq market on the day of its initial public offering in New York on July 10. REUTERS/YONHAP SK hynix's ADR is the first real test of whether the market will revalue a Korean memory chipmaker as a U.S.-listed AI infrastructure asset, according to Kim Doo-un, a senior analyst at Hana Securities. "If the ADR premium holds and memory earnings remain intact, the recent pullback should be viewed not as the end of the bull market but as a pause before a second upswing,” Kim said. While the stock sank, SK hynix’s U.S. listing is expected to bolster the won, providing relief for one of the Korean authorities’ biggest economic headaches. The chip giant said part of the $26.5 billion in proceeds it raised from ADR will be invested in Korea. In a regulatory filing for the ADR last month, SK hynix said the proceeds will be used to build chip fabrication plants in Yongin, Gyeonggi, an advanced packaging fab in Cheongju in North Chungcheong and to purchase chipmaking equipment such as extreme ultraviolet scanners. The dollar inflow exceeds the $19.87 billion currency swap line Korea secured from the United States during the 2020 pandemic crisis and is nearly double the roughly $13.6 billion the foreign exchange authorities sold in the market in the first quarter to support the won. The local currency was trading at 1,503.4 won against the dollar at 3:30 p.m on Monday, compared to 1,501.4 won from the previous session. "Although the size and timing of the currency conversion have yet to be determined, the inflow is expected to have a significant impact on foreign exchange market supply and demand," said Park Seok-hyun, the deputy head of the wealth management products division at Woori Bank, deviating from many exporting firms at times of foreign exchange volatility with "plans to repatriate a substantial portion of the proceeds for domestic investment rather than hold them in U.S. dollars." BY JIN MIN-JI [jin.minji@joongang.co.kr] chip business adr sk hynix stock semiconductor kospi money

records.excerpt: The S&P 500 remains firmly entrenched in a long-term uptrend, trading within a well-defined ascending channel and comfortably above both Share Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Pinterest Email Tumblr Reddit Telegram WhatsApp Copy Link S&P 500 Tests Record Highs, Bulls Eye Next Leg The S&P 500 remains firmly entrenched in a long-term uptrend, trading within a well-defined ascending channel and comfortably above both its 200-day and 200-week simple moving averages, according to a brief released by one of South Africa’s largest banks. While overall market sentiment has softened slightly, the broader backdrop remains neutral rather than bearish, with investors balancing geopolitical risks, inflation concerns, and shifting central bank expectations. The index is now testing a key resistance level near 7 620, placing markets at an important technical inflexion point, First National Bank (FNB) said in a brief on Monday, The bank said from a technical perspective, a decisive break above 7 620 would confirm the continuation of the current Elliott Wave 5 advance, potentially opening the way towards the upper boundary of the channel near 8 280. Failure to break higher could trigger a period of consolidation or correction, with initial support located near 7 020 and stronger support around 6 560, should selling pressure intensify. Despite these risks, the primary trend remains constructive as long as the index holds above key support levels. “The outlook remains broadly positive, with our AI-generated forecast model pointing to continued strength over the medium term”. While some consolidation is expected over the coming months, the technical picture suggests that the current move is more consistent with a pause within an ongoing bull market rather than the beginning of a sustained downturn, FNB added. For investors, it said the key signal to watch is whether the index can successfully clear 7 620, which would reinforce the case for another leg higher in one of the strongest equity rallies of recent years. records.excerpt: Title: Berkshire Hathaway gains ground, but still trails the S&P 500 as '26 enters second half URL Source: http://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/11/berkshire-hathaway-gains-ground-but-still-trails-the-sp-500-as-26-enters-second-half.html Published Time: 2026-07-11T13:07:41+0000 Markdown Content: _(This is the Warren Buffett Watch newsletter, news and analysis on all things Warren Buffett and Berkshire Hathaway. You can sign up_[_here_](https://www.cnbc.com/sign-up-for-cnbc-newsletters?__source=newsletter%7Cwarrenbuffettwatch)_to receive it every Friday evening in your inbox.)_ ## [](http://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/11/berkshire-hathaway-gains-ground-but-still-trails-the-sp-500-as-26-enters-second-half.html)Berkshire gains ground but still trails S&P as ’26 enters second half With 2026 a bit more than half over, Berkshire Hathaway’s[B shares](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/BRK.B/)are down 1.8% year-to-date and 12.4 percentage points behind the[S&P 500′s](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.SPX/)10.7% gain. (Including dividends, the S&P is up 11.4% giving it a 13.1 percentage point lead). A[strong June](https://link.cnbc.com/public/46423350)for Berkshire erased almost a third of its 17.5 percentage point deficit as of June 1, its biggest losing margin of the year so far. ![Image 1](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108333697-1783735543522-2026-07-10_berkshire-b-shares-vs-s-amp-p-2026-.png?v=1783735557&vtcrop=y) Even with that June bump, however, it’s been a tough Q2 (+ 10 days) for Berkshire with a gain of a bit more than 3% versus the benchmark’s strong[tech-driven](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/09/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)16% advance, totally erasing what was a slim 1.8 percentage point Berkshire lead at the end of March. ![Image 2](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108333698-1783735594984-2026-07-10_BRK_SPX_since_April_1.png?v=1783735613&vtcrop=y) Last year,[Berkshire underperformed](https://link.cnbc.com/public/43308222)the S&P by 5.5 percentage points excluding dividends. The deficit was 7.0 percentage points with dividends included. ## [](http://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/11/berkshire-hathaway-gains-ground-but-still-trails-the-sp-500-as-26-enters-second-half.html)Berkshire execs spotted at exclusive Sun Valley conference Berkshire Hathaway CEO Greg Abel and portfolio manager Ted Weschler aren’t featured in the[_Forbes_ article](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jimdobson/2026/07/06/sun-valleys-billionaire-summer-camp-returns-bezos-zuckerberg-and-altman-lead-the-pack/?__source=newsletter%7Cwarrenbuffettwatch)on “Sun Valley’s Billionaire Summer Camp” now underway in Idaho. But they are on the magazine’s list of attendees and photos from CNBC’s David Grogan and Brendan McDermid of _Reuters_ provide visual evidence they are present at the annual Allen & Co. invitation-only gathering of moguls, along with names like Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg, and Sam Altman. Greg Abel, President and CEO of Berkshire Hathaway arrives at the annual Allen & Co. Media and Technology Conference in Sun Valley, Idaho on July 8, 2026. David A. Grogan | CNBC Ted Weschler, portfolio manager for Berkshire Hathaway Inc., attends the annual Allen and Co. Sun Valley Media and Technology Conference at the Sun Valley Resort in Sun Valley, Idaho, U.S., July 8, 2026. REUTERS/Brendan McDermid Warren Buffett went to Sun Valley for decades but has not attended the last few years. In 1999, at the height of the dotcom craze, he gave a[notable speech at the conference](https://www.berkshirehathaway.com/1999ar/FortuneMagazine.pdf?__source=newsletter%7Cwarrenbuffettwatch)warning that while the internet would be transformative, investors were expecting too much and were bound to be disappointed. ## [](http://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/11/berkshire-hathaway-gains-ground-but-still-trails-the-sp-500-as-26-enters-second-half.html)BUFFETT & BERKSHIRE AROUND THE INTERNET ## [](http://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/11/berkshire-hathaway-gains-ground-but-still-trails-the-sp-500-as-26-enters-second-half.html)HIGHLIGHTS FROM CNBC’S BUFFETT ARCHIVE ## [](http://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/11/berkshire-hathaway-gains-ground-but-still-trails-the-sp-500-as-26-enters-second-half.html)AI could make financial scams a ‘growth industry’ (2024) [Warren Buffett describes](https://buffett.cnbc.com/video/2024/05/06/ai-could-make-financial-scams-a-growth-industry.html)seeing a convincing AI-generated video of himself that has him worried the technology will make financial scams much more effective. ![Image 3: AI could make financial scams a 'growth industry'](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/107410699-1714923062BUFFETT-Archive-050424-Clips-2.jpg?v=1714923060&w=750&h=422&vtcrop=y) watch now **AUDIENCE MEMBER**:How do you think about the role of technological advances, especially generative AI, on more traditional industries? Thank you... **WARREN BUFFETT**: I don’t know anything about AI. But I do — I do have — I don’t — that doesn’t mean I deny its existence or importance or anything of the sort. And last year I said, you know, that we let the genie out of the bottle when we developed nuclear weapons, and that genie has been doing some terrible things lately. And the power of that genie is what, you know, scares the hell out of me. And on, the other hand, I don’t know any way to get the genie back in the bottle. And AI is somewhat similar. It’s out — it’s part-way out of the bottle. And it’s enormously important, and it’s going to be done by somebody... Now AI, I had one experience that does make me a little nervous. And I’ll just explain it. Very recently — fairly recently — I saw an image in front of my eyes on the screen, and it was me, and it was my voice and wearing the kind of clothes I wear. And my wife or my daughter wouldn’t have been able to detect any difference. And it was delivering a message that no way came from me. So — it — when you think of the potential for scamming people, if you can reproduce images that I can’t even tell, that say, I need money, you know, it’s your daughter, I’ve just had a car crash. I need fifty thousand dollars wired. I mean, scamming has always been part of the American scene. But this would make me, if I was interested in investing in scamming, it’s going to be the growth industry of all time. And it’s enabled in a way — you know, obviously AI has potential for good things, too, but I don’t know how you — based on the one I saw recently, I practically would send money to myself over in some crazy country. (Laughter) So I don’t have any advice on how the world handles it because I don’t think we know how to handle what we did with the nuclear genie. records.title: AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ: ASTS) Hits Rare Inflection Point As Satellites Launch And FCC Clears Commercial Service
records.excerpt: AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ: ASTS) has spent years as a compelling story without the operational track record to match, but 2026 is shaping up to be the year that AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ: ASTS) has spent years as a compelling story without the operational track record to match, but 2026 is shaping up to be the year that changes. The company’s core proposition is straightforward but ambitious: beam broadband connectivity directly to ordinary, unmodified smartphones from satellites in orbit. Submit a Press Release or News Tip That vision cleared its most significant regulatory hurdle in May, when the FCC authorized AST SpaceMobile to run commercial SpaceMobile Service in the United States. The FCC approval removed what had long been the single biggest barrier standing between the company and paying customers in the American market. Then, in June, AST SpaceMobile followed up that regulatory win with the launch of three additional BlueBird satellites, the large orbital arrays responsible for connecting directly to phones on the ground. The company is targeting approximately 45 satellites in orbit during 2026, a threshold that will define whether the network can begin functioning as a genuine commercial product. Partnerships with AT&T and Verizon represent another meaningful de-risking factor, allowing AST to extend existing cellular networks rather than build a standalone customer base from scratch. Those carrier relationships reduce commercialization risk considerably and provide a route to revenue that does not depend on consumers signing up for an entirely new service. Investors should weigh the risks carefully, however, as reaching full global coverage will require many more launches, and satellite construction and deployment remain expensive undertakings. The company has repeatedly raised cash by issuing new shares, diluting existing shareholders, and competition from Starlink’s own direct-to-cell effort adds further pressure on timing and market share. Launches can slip, hardware can fail, and any one of those setbacks could stall momentum at precisely the moment the business case is coming into focus. The investment case therefore comes down to recognizing, as one analysis put it, that AST SpaceMobile is at a rare inflection point where “a speculative concept either becomes a working network or doesn’t.” For investors with a genuine tolerance for volatility and the possibility of total loss, a small and deliberate position sized accordingly may be more appropriate than chasing the stock after the next major headline. The next couple of quarters carry more weight than any single earnings report, and the window for acting ahead of an obvious outcome may be narrower than it appears. Share: Tags:

records.title: Federal Funds Rate History 1990 to 2026
records.excerpt: Title: Federal Funds Rate History 1990 to 2026 URL Source: http://www.forbes.com/advisor/investing/fed-funds-rate-history-1/ Published Time: 2024-05-20T13:28:07-04:00 Markdown Content: The Federal Reserve has battled a variety of economic troubles over the past 35 years. Between tech busts, a financial crisis and a pandemic, not to mention periods of too little inflation and too much, the nation’s central bank has used short-term interest rates, along with other more novel measures, to fulfill its reason for being: Keep prices stable and maximize unemployment. As the Fed currently endeavors to wind down inflation without causing a recession, it is useful to see how and why it acted in the past. Forbes Advisor has compiled this history as a handy guide to the course of the federal funds rate and the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy decisions since 1990. ## Understanding Fed Interest Rate Decisions The federal funds rate is the main lever the Federal Reserve uses to manage the economy. In keeping with its mandate, the Fed prefers inflation to be 2% and for the labor market to be as fully employed as possible without causing inflation to go beyond that target rate. Should prices rise too slowly (like in the 2010s), the Fed will lower rates to spur economic growth. The theory is that lower rates incentivize more economic activity because banks are more likely to lend cash than let it sit on the sidelines earning meager returns. Conversely, when prices rise too quickly (like in the aftermath of the pandemic), the Fed will raise rates in order to stymie economic activity. The unemployment rate will tend to rise (as has happened over the past year or so), as businesses find it harder to invest. The Fed, though, doesn’t just rely on inflation and employment metrics to devise its monetary policy. It considers all sorts of indicators, from housing starts to consumer spending, to gauge just how well the economy is performing. It will act quickly in the face of unforeseen events, such as a global pandemic or terrorist attack. While Congress holds the purse strings, market participants look to how and why the Fed acts when placing their bets on the future. ### About the Data The tables below list the dates of Fed meetings when the Federal Open Market Committee changed interest rates, the size of each rate change in basis points—abbreviated as bps—and the resulting federal funds target rate range. Basis points are a common unit of measurement for interest rates. One basis point is equal to 1/100 th of one percentage point, or 0.01%. For instance, a half a percentage point change in an interest rate would equal 50 basis points. Please note that before 1990, the Fed didn’t explicitly target a set federal funds rate. If you’re interested in earlier rate policy, look through this [Federal Reserve document](https://www.federalreserve.gov/foia/files/20190829-changes-intended-federal-funds-rate.pdf) produced through a Freedom of Information Act request. ## Fed Rate Cuts 2024-2026: Still Taming Inflation The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.50%–3.75% following the June FOMC meeting. Bank economists say we’re seeing a “hawkish Federal Reserve,” with half of the committee expecting a rate hike this year. The new Fed chair, Kevin Warsh, stepped to the podium for the first time following the FOMC June meeting. Warsh took office as the chairman of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve in May 2026. Warsh refrained from offering any forward projection of his own because of his long-held views on the Summary of Economic Projections (SEP), as it’s currently structured. “In the medium projection, real GDP rises by 2.2% this year and 2.3%,” he said, adding that “inflation is a choice.” The philosophy of “inflation is a choice” pushes back against blaming price increases solely on global supply chain disruptions or specific commodity shortages. Instead, it asserts that these are one-time price adjustments, and true inflation stems from broader monetary policy decisions. According to ING research, business surveys indicate GDP growth of 2% to 2.5% amid rising inflation. Expectations for future Federal Reserve rate hikes have grown amid rising headline inflation. “Inflation remains elevated relative to the committee’s 2% goal, in part reflecting supply shocks that have driven price increases in certain sectors, including energy,” according to the FOMC’s June news release. The Iran war is complicating matters for the Fed, with soaring oil and gas prices. Higher energy prices could have a ripple effect on other costs, like food and utilities. The market is pricing in at least one rate hike before year-end. ### 2024-2025 In 2025, there were three consecutive 25-basis-point rate cuts: one at the September FOMC meeting, another at the October meeting, and a third in December. | FOMC Meeting Date | Rate Change (Bps) | Federal Funds Rate | | --- | --- | --- | | Dec. 10, 2025 | -25 | 3.50% to 3.75% | | Oct 29, 2025 | -25 | 3.75% to 4.00% | | Sept 17, 2025 | -25 | 4.00% to 4.25% | | Dec 18, 2024 | -25 | 4.25% to 4.50% | | Nov 7, 2024 | -25 | 4.50% to 4.75% | | Sept 18, 2024 | -50 | 4.75% to 5.00% | ## Fed Rate Hikes 2022-2023: Taming Inflation and Beyond | FOMC Meeting Date | Rate Change (bps) | Federal Funds Rate | | --- | --- | --- | | July 26, 2023 | +25 | 5.25% to 5.50% | | May 3, 2023 | +25 | 5.00% to 5.25% | | March 22, 2023 | +25 | 4.75% to 5.00% | | Feb 1, 2023 | +25 | 4.50% to 4.75% | | Dec 14, 2022 | +50 | 4.25% to 4.50% | | Nov 2, 2022 | +75 | 3.75% to 4.00% | | Sept 21, 2022 | +75 | 3.00% to 3.25% | | July 27, 2022 | +75 | 2.25% to 2.50% | | June 16, 2022 | +75 | 1.50% to 1.75% | | May 5, 2022 | +50 | 0.75% to 1.00% | In early 2022, the Fed was keeping the federal funds rate as low as possible and buying billions of bonds each month to prop up the economy. Remember, inflation was soaring for the better part of a year. But when the Fed realized that inflation was going to be [much less transitory](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/why-was-the-fed-so-wrong-about-inflation) than it imagined, it shifted gears forcefully. Between March 2022 and July 2023, the Fed raised rates by more than five percentage points. “Without price stability, the economy does not work for anyone,” Powell said at an August 2022 speech at Jackson Hole. “In particular, without price stability, we will not achieve a sustained period of strong labor market conditions that benefit all.” The tough medicine had the desired effect, up to a point. Inflation, using the Fed’s preferred metric, dropped from 6.6% in September 2022 to 2.6% in March 2025. ## 2020 Fed Rate Cuts: Coping with Covid-19 | FOMC Meeting Date | Rate Change (bps) | Federal Funds Rate | | --- | --- | --- | | March 16, 2020 | -100 | 0% to 0.25% | | March 3, 2020 | -50 | 1.0% to 1.25% | “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) met in December indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate.” So began the FOMC’s policy statement on Jan. 29, 2020, just a few days before the U.S. economy plunged into the Covid-19 recession. The Covid-19 pandemic would spread across the globe weeks later, leading to public health officials worldwide recommending lockdowns to stop the spread of the virus and ease hospital caseloads. Roughly 20.5 million jobs would be shed in April 2020 alone, with the unemployment rate jumping to 14.7%. The FOMC delivered two huge rate cuts at unscheduled emergency meetings in March 2020, returning the federal funds target rate range of zero to 0.25%. While the economy was technically growing again by May 2020, after the shortest recession on record, the fallout from the economic measures to cope with the Covid-19 outbreak is still being felt today. ## 2019 Fed Rate Cuts: Mid-Cycle Adjustment | FOMC Meeting Date | Rate Change (bps) | Federal Funds Rate | | --- | --- | --- | | October 31, 2019 | -25 | 1.50% to 1.75%

records.title: SpaceX Joins Nasdaq-100, Giving Many 401(k)s Exposure
records.excerpt: SpaceX Joins Nasdaq-100, Giving Many 401(k)s Exposure Facebook Linkedin X Youtube Practice Products Fiduciary Regulation Social Security Events SECURE Pod(k)ast Deep Dive Partner Leaders Speak Sponsored Articles Advertise About About Us Contact Us Digital Edition Archive Reprints and Licensing Editorial Policies 401(k) Specialist News for Retirement Advisors Subscribe Get our email newsletter Prefer us on Google 401(k) Specialist News for Retirement Advisors Subscribe Practice Products Fiduciary Regulation Social Security Events SECURE Pod(k)ast Deep Dive Partner Leaders Speak Sponsored Articles Advertise About About Us Contact Us Digital Edition Archive Reprints and Licensing Editorial Policies 401(k) Specialist News for Retirement Advisors Practice Products Fiduciary Regulation Social Security Events SECURE Pod(k)ast Deep Dive Partner Leaders Speak Sponsored Articles Advertise About About Us Contact Us Digital Edition Archive Reprints and Licensing Editorial Policies Subscribe Topics Your 401(k) News Many 401(k) Participants Now Own SpaceX—Whether They Know It or Not SpaceX's record-fast addition to the Nasdaq-100 means millions of retirement savers now have indirect exposure to the newly public company through index funds and some target-date portfolios By Brian Anderson | July 10, 2026 | 4 minute read Share Linkedin X Facebook Email Copy URL Prefer us on Google Image credit: © Saulo Angelo | Dreamstime.com A lot of 401(k)s now hold positions in SpaceX after the company’s potentially volatile stock was added to the Nasdaq-100 on July 7, less than a month after its historic June 12 initial public offering. It is the fastest new inclusion in the index’s history. The Nasdaq-100 , a tech-heavy index tracking the 100 largest non-financial stocks traded on the Nasdaq exchange, includes many companies with high growth prospects. In anticipation of a trio of high-profile mega-IPOs (Spacex, OpenAI and Anthropic), the Nasdaq and benchmark indexes offered by FTSE Russell and MSCI in May announced updated eligibility requirements for a stock to be included in their flagship indexes. The changes allow stocks to be eligible to join the indexes just days after an IPO, compared to a previous wait period of at least three months. SpaceX was added to the Russell 1000 (and Russell Top 200) after June 26 and started trading June 29, triggered automatic buying by every fund tracking those indexes. S&P Dow Jones Indices did not change its methodology rules, so SpaceX will not be eligible to join the S&P 500 for at least a year. In order to eventually be included in the S&P 500, SpaceX would need to register four quarters of profits—something it took another Elon Musk company—Tesla—10 years to do. According to CNN , there are over 200 investment products with $800 billion in assets that track the Nasdaq-100. One popular example is the QQQ exchange-traded fund from Invesco that has roughly $480 billion in total investments. That means QQQ investors own shares of SpaceX, without doing anything on their own. Funds that track the index have to buy SpaceX in order to continue mirroring its performance. That means investors who hold Nasdaq 100-related funds will automatically gain exposure to SpaceX—something a lot of 401(k) participants are probably completely unaware of, as index funds passively buy and hold securities in the same proportions as the index they follow. Participants invested in Nasdaq-100 index funds—or diversified funds that hold Nasdaq-100 exposure—likely now indirectly own SpaceX. It is important to note that most 401(k) exposure to the Musk-led rocket, connectivity and AI company is small for now. The company went public with less than 5% of its shares available for trading, meaning its weight in the index is starting out much smaller than its true market value. Not every 401(k) participant will gain exposure to SpaceX. Participants will only own shares indirectly if they invest in a fund that tracks the Nasdaq-100 or another index or investment strategy that includes the stock. Many retirement plans instead use S&P 500, Russell 3000, or total-market index funds, which may have different exposure depending on the index methodology. The inclusion also raises questions for plan fiduciaries about how quickly newly public companies should become part of retirement portfolios. While index providers have shortened waiting periods to reflect today’s IPO market, some fiduciaries may question whether newly public companies have sufficient trading history before becoming part of default retirement investments. That means not every retirement portfolio owns SpaceX simply because it’s in the Nasdaq-100. Active managers may underweight it, avoid it entirely, or wait for more trading history before purchasing shares. Participants in a target-date fund that utilizes total-market or Nasdaq-100 index sleeves, will own a tiny, heavily diluted slice of SpaceX. According to wealth advisor Madison Partners , if your target-date fund has a 60% stock allocation and SpaceX makes up 0.5% of the equity sleeve, that’s 0.3% of your total retirement balance. On a $500,000 portfolio, that’s $1,500. Per CNN, someone owning $100 worth of the Nasdaq 100 would own about $1 worth of SpaceX shares. SpaceX’s weighting in the Nasdaq 100 could increase significantly over time as more shares become available for trading as lock-up periods expire and the supply of shares on the market increases. SpaceX closes first month of trading SpaceX ( Nasdaq: SPCX ) on Friday essentially completed its first month of trading pretty close to where it started. SpaceX priced its debut at $135 but commenced trading at $150 on June 12. The stock gained 19% in its debut session, closing at $161, briefly topped $200 on June 16 and finished June just under $171, but has since fallen back below where it opened. SpaceX closed Friday at $145.30, down 4.51% for the day. ETFs for anti-Elon crowd SpaceX’s Elon Musk. Image credit: © Frédéric Legrand | Dreamstime.com For investors wanting to steer clear for various reasons of supporting Elon Musk-led ventures, TechCrunch reports there are two new exchange-traded funds (ETFs) that specifically exclude his companies. An ETF creator called Subversive Capital introduced Nasdaq-100 Ex-Elon Enterprises ETF and S&P 500 Ex-Elon Enterprises ETF, both of which are designed to block SpaceX and Tesla (Musk’s other companies, including Neuralink and The Boring Company, are not publicly traded). The Ex-Elon funds seek “to provide capital appreciation through exposure to a broad universe of large-capitalization U.S. equity securities, while excluding the equity securities of companies that are founded, controlled, or led by Elon Musk, or with which Mr. Musk is otherwise primarily associated,” states the document filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, per TechCrunch. records.title: SK Hynix Joins the Nasdaq. But This Nasdaq-100 Semiconductor Stock Could Be an Even Better Buy for the Second Half of 2026.
records.excerpt: As of market close on July 9, the seven best-performing S&P 500 ( ^GSPC +0.42% ) stocks year to date are Sandisk , Dell Technologies , Micron Technology , Western Digital , Seagate Technology Holdings , Intel , and Marvell Technology . All of these companies are directly involved with or benefiting from the boom in memory chips for artificial intelligence (AI) workloads in data centers and consumer electronics. Demand for memory chips and energy are the two greatest bottlenecks impacting the AI industry right now . High bandwidth memory (HBM) and dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips function as a working memory for handling massive AI training and inference data sets. And AI NAND (flash) supports longer-term, large-scale data storage and use. SK Hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY) (NASDAQ: SKHYV) is a full-stack AI memory provider. It is expanding its HBM capabilities to improve AI chip performance. Demand for SK Hynix memory chips is far outpacing supply, creating a multi-year runway for future growth that has propelled the company to a $1 trillion valuation . On Friday, July 10, SK Hynix listed on the Nasdaq after launching a U.S. share sale . SK Hynix is up 241.5% year to date as of market close on July 9. If it were in the S&P 500, it would be the fourth-best-performing stock, ahead of Western Digital and right behind its competitor Micron. SK Hynix will never join the S&P 500 because it's a South Korean company, just as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing isn't in the S&P 500. However, it will likely be fast-tracked into the Nasdaq-100 over the coming weeks, similar to how Space Exploration Technologies ( SPCX 4.51% ) went public on June 12 and was added to the Nasdaq-100 on July 7 . The Nasdaq-100 is the 100 largest non-financial companies by market cap listed on the Nasdaq exchange. SK Hynix is chock-full of potential. But ASML ( ASML 0.40% ) is an even better Nasdaq-100 stock for investors looking for a fundamental AI stock to buy and hold for at least five years . Image source: Getty Images. ASML is in a league of its own Netherlands-based ASML is the most valuable company in Europe. And although it's not in the S&P 500 because it isn't based in the U.S., it is one of the top 15 largest holdings in the Nasdaq-100. ASML doesn't design or manufacture chips. Rather, it produces highly advanced machines needed to perform the lithography step in the semiconductor manufacturing process. Lithography is arguably the most complex and important step in the chip production process because it involves printing designs onto silicon. ASML has a virtual monopoly on extreme ultraviolet (EUV) machines that use reflective lenses to bounce light in a vacuum, rather than refracting it. The EUV technology produces an incredibly short 13.5-nanometer (nm) wavelength, compared to around 193 nm for deep ultraviolet (DUV) machines. ASML's high-numerical-aperture (High-NA) EUV machines have an even higher resolution for producing next-generation AI chips at scale. Shorter wavelengths enable chip manufacturers to print smaller, denser features on critical microchip layers in a single pass. To achieve that same level of precision, DUV machines use a process called multi-patterning, which involves several steps and takes longer. So even though EUV machines are incredibly expensive, they can be higher-performance and more cost-effective over a longer useful life. You can think of DUV machines like manually hitting a nail with a hammer, and EUV machines as having a nail gun. If you're hanging a painting up, a hammer is just fine. But if you're building a house, you'd want the nail gun. EUV machines are overpowered for general chip manufacturing that doesn't require small transistors and wires. But they play an integral role in AI chip manufacturing. There are multiple companies besides ASML that make DUV machines. But ASML is the one that cracked the code on EUV machines, giving chip designers the nail gun needed to evolve manufacturing from nomadic bands to a booming civilization. As AI adoption grows, fabs that are taking AI chip orders will need to upgrade their equipment to ASML's more advanced EUV machines. And newer fabs will likely incorporate EUV machines as standard equipment. Just last month, Elon Musk addressed ASML employees during a conversation with ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet about the proposed Terafab joint venture between Tesla ( TSLA +0.22% ) , SpaceX, and SpaceX-owned xAI. Terafab would be the largest chip manufacturing facility -- tasked with producing AI chips for SpaceX's orbital data centers . Since Terafab would be handling AI chip workloads, it would need ASML's most advanced machines. And given ASML's multi-year backlog , Musk was essentially giving ASML the green light to accelerate production, since big orders could be coming down the road. But no company comes close to challenging ASML in EUV lithography. Best of all, ASML's lithography machines are needed to produce all kinds of AI chips, including logic chips such as graphics processing units (GPUs), central processing units, and custom-built AI chips like Alphabet 's Tensor Processing Units and HBM, DRAM, and NAND memory chips like those made by SK Hynix. Each quarter, ASML breaks down net system sales (equipment orders excluding servicing its installed base) by logic and memory. In the first quarter of 2026, memory jumped to 51% compared to 42% in the first quarter of 2025, while logic declined from 58% to 49%. The beauty of ASML's business model is that it wins as long as AI chip demand is growing. It is relatively indifferent whether custom AI chips, like those made by Alphabet, eat into GPU market share. Or if Intel takes market share from Taiwan Semiconductor, SK Hynix gains an edge over Micron, etc. ASML has already benefited from the insatiable demand for AI compute, and it is now also benefiting from the boom in memory chip demand. In sum, buying SK Hynix is a pure-play bet on memory chip demand continuing to outpace supply and on SK Hynix holding its own against fierce competition. Buying ASML is a catch-all way to bet on increased AI chip innovation and the need for higher production, and in turn, more ASML machines in chip fabs. ASML is worth the premium price ASML's position in the AI supply chain is well known. The stock is up 125% over the last year and trades at a premium valuation, with a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 49.5, compared with 49.2 for Applied Materials and 43.5 for Lam Research. ASML may need its earnings growth to catch up to its valuation to justify a higher run-up. But for investors with a long-term time horizon, it stands out as arguably the best semiconductor stock to buy and hold because next-generation AI logic and memory chips depend on ASML's systems to bring their designs to life.

records.title: If I Could Tell Every QQQ Investor 1 Thing About SpaceX's Nasdaq-100 Entry, It's This
records.excerpt: Space Exploration Technologies ( SPCX 4.51% ) joined the Nasdaq-100 index on July 7. If you own the Invesco QQQ ETF ( QQQ +0.31% ) or the Invesco Nasdaq 100 ETF ( QQQM +0.32% ) , you now own a piece of it too. SpaceX has gotten a lot of attention since its initial public offering (IPO). But now that it's getting added to major market indexes, the most important step is assessing its impact. What might surprise many people is that, despite its massive $2 trillion market cap, the stock isn't nearly as influential in the Nasdaq-100 as you might think. And that's perhaps the biggest takeaway from this story. Image source: Getty Images. SpaceX isn't even a top-20 holding in the Nasdaq-100 The reason SpaceX has only a relatively minor influence on the index is the distinction between total market capitalization and free-float market capitalization. Free-float market cap takes into account only the shares that are publicly available. For SpaceX, that's about 5% of the total shares available. Most companies only have a percentage of their total shares publicly tradable, but SpaceX has less than average. By total market cap, SpaceX would rank as one of the 10 largest companies in the world. But because the Nasdaq-100 uses free-float market cap, it's only the 21st-largest holding in the index, between KLA and Texas Instruments . Its weight is 1.25%. SpaceX won't have a meaningful impact on the Nasdaq-100 If you're buying either the Invesco QQQ ETF or the Invesco Nasdaq 100 ETF expecting a significant stake in SpaceX, you're probably going to be disappointed. Even a major rally or crash in the stock market likely won't be felt in the index. The one thing to potentially be mindful of is the volatility of the stock. The IPO price was set at $135. It initially traded at around $150 when it went public, reached as high as $225, and is now back down to around $149. There's a lot of noise in the trading behavior of this stock. From investors trying to get their hands on shares for the first time to the fund industry buying millions of shares to track their underlying indexes, volatility in SpaceX could be higher than average for a while until things settle a bit. The next big milestone will be next summer when the stock becomes eligible for inclusion in the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC +0.42% ) . While there will be another wave of buying if and when that happens, expectations should be tempered on that day as well. The S&P 500 is also free-float, market-cap-weighted, and might receive an even smaller allocation there.

records.excerpt: These overlooked consumer stocks could offer investors more dependable paths to long-term returns than the newly public megacap. On July 7, Space Exploration Technologies ( SPCX 4.51% ) became one of the newest members of the Nasdaq-100 , added just 15 trading days after its record-setting public debut under a new fast-entry rule. Roughly $800 billion sits in funds that track that index, so every one of them had to buy the stock , and that mechanical demand has grabbed a lot of headlines. Here's the thing worth remembering: A stock may meet the criteria to be added to a prominent index, but that doesn't necessarily make it a good buy. Forced buying by passively managed funds can inflate the price of a freshly public, richly valued stock in the short term, but history is full of hyped-up index additions that later proved to be disappointing investments. Rather than chase the rocket, I'd point patient investors toward three quieter Nasdaq-100 members in the consumer world that are doing genuinely interesting things right now. records.title: iShares Ethereum Trust ETF vs Hashdex Nasdaq Crypto Index ETF: Is Diversification a Winning Crypto Strategy?
records.excerpt: One fund bets on Ether alone; the other diversifies across Bitcoin and other digital assets. Both charge 0.25% but differ sharply in scale and volatility. The choice between the iShares Ethereum Trust ETF ( ETHA +2.58% ) and the Hashdex Nasdaq Crypto Index US ETF ( NCIQ +1.11% ) hinges on whether an investor seeks pure exposure to one digital asset or a diversified crypto index. The iShares fund provides a targeted bet on the Ethereum ( ETH 1.49% ) ecosystem, while the Hashdex fund tracks a market-cap-weighted index of Bitcoin ( BTC 1.92% ) and other prominent digital assets.
