The 1-yr return represents total return over the trailing 12 months. Both funds are competitively priced with an expense ratio of 0.25%, which is at the lower end for crypto ETFs . They differ considerably in scale as the iShares fund manages $4.9 billion in assets under management (AUM), offering significantly higher liquidity than the Hashdex fund. Performance & risk comparison Metric NCIQ ETHA Max drawdown (1 yr) (57.05%) (67.91%) Growth of $1,000 over 1 year (total return) $512 $478 What's inside The iShares Ethereum Trust ETF maintains a singular focus, holding just Ethereum. The fund was launched in 2024 and provides investors with a way to gain exposure to the popular coin without the complexities of managing digital wallets or private keys. The fund has quickly gained scale, currently managing approximately $4.9 billion in AUM. Launched in 2025, the fund’s largest positions include Bitcoin at 78.5%, Ethereum at 11.4%, and Ripple’s XRP ( XRP 2.03% ) at 5.3%. The fund manages roughly $206 million in AUM and rebalances quarterly. NASDAQ : NCIQ Hashdex Nasdaq Crypto Index Us Etf Today's Change ( 1.11 %) $ 0.17 Current Price $ 15.90 Key Data Points AUM $99M Expense Ratio 0.25% Both funds invest in spot assets rather than using leverage to amplify crypto positions. Neither fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940, so they are exempt from certain regulatory requirements that apply to traditional mutual funds. For more guidance on ETF investing, check out the full guide at this link . What it means for investors Both Bitcoin and Ethereum soared to new highs in 2025, but crypto prices have fallen significantly this year. That volatility is, unfortunately, to be expected in crypto investing, which is why it is advisable to allocate only a small percentage of your portfolio to digital assets. When it comes to these two ETFs, the real question is which cryptocurrencies you want to invest in. Bear in mind that cryptocurrencies are very different from stocks because it is still a relatively new industry, and once you go beyond the main two (Bitcoin and Ethereum), the risk increases dramatically. A fund like NCIQ that tracks major coins and tokens is not the same as, say, an index fund that tracks the S&P 500 . Ethereum and Bitcoin jointly account for over 90% of the Hashdex fund, while the iShares ETF is totally dedicated to Ethereum. Ethereum pioneered the technology that makes blockchains programmable and still accounts for the lion’s share of decentralized finance applications. Bitcoin is the original cryptocurrency and has attracted a large share of institutional investment, particularly as some view it as a form of digital gold — though the store-of-value thesis has yet to be proven. Both Bitcoin and Ethereum have a role in a balanced crypto portfolio, and if you want a way to buy the two together, the Hashdex ETF does the job. However, I am not keen on the automatic exposure to other, riskier cryptocurrencies, even though they only make up 10% of the fund. You would get more control by investing in a spot Ethereum ETF like ETHA alongside a 100% spot Bitcoin ETF .

records.title: Jesuits will create 2 novitiates from 5 current US and Canada novitiates
records.excerpt: Title: Jesuits will create 2 novitiates from 5 current US and Canada novitiates URL Source: http://www.ncronline.org/news/jesuits-will-create-2-novitiates-5-current-us-and-canada-novitiates Published Time: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:03:08 GMT Markdown Content: DETROIT — July 11, 2026 The Society of Jesus — commonly known as the Jesuits — in the United States and Canada will bring together its five current novitiates spread throughout the continent into two new novitiates starting in 2028, with one of the new novitiates to be located in Detroit. The Jesuit Conference of Canada and the United States, which includes five Jesuit provinces in North America, announced the change in a letter sent July 9 to members of the religious community. According to the letter, which was signed by the leaders of the five North American provinces, the Detroit-based novitiate will be located at Lansing-Reilly Hall, the Jesuit residence on the campus of the University of Detroit Mercy. In addition to hosting the novices from the Midwest province — which is based in Chicago — the Detroit novitiate will also host novices from the U.S. Eastern Province and the Canada Province. The other novitiate will be based in Culver City, California, at the current location of the novitiate for the Jesuits' West province, the Novitiate of the Three Companions. Besides hosting novices from the Jesuits West, it will host novices from the U.S. Central and Southern provinces. The "multi-province" model, as the society's leadership calls it, would "allow us to maintain robust cohorts of novices and provide them with the best formators we could," the provincials said in the letter. Both novitiates are expected to accommodate up to 30 novices, with the sites ready by summer 2028. Jesuit Fr. Joseph Daoust, superior of the Detroit Jesuit community, said the rearrangement of novitiates will ensure each location has an adequate number of novices for a proper formation experience, and it will free up other members of the Jesuits for different works in the society. "Running five novitiates takes an awful lot of Jesuit staff of very good people," Daoust told Detroit Catholic, the news outlet of the Archdiocese of Detroit. "You have to have three or four Jesuits in each of the novitiates, who usually are more senior Jesuits who serve as the formators of the novices. If we could put the novices in only two novitiates rather than five, we would save an awful lot of very valuable manpower for other works of the Society of Jesus." Daoust added that the number of novices entering each of the five current novitiates fluctuates "quite a bit" from year to year, with anywhere from one to 12 new novices per year. Consolidation will allow the Jesuits to maintain steady numbers in each of the two new novitiates, including the opportunity to move novices back and forth between novitiates as necessary. Novitiates host novices for their first two years of religious formation "in the spirituality of St. Ignatius of Loyola," Daoust said. "It takes two years of formation before they can make permanent vows of poverty, chastity and obedience," he explained. "So the men living here are not technically religious in the full sense; they haven’t taken vows, and they can leave at any time if they want. But they’re here to be trained in order to become vowed Jesuits, members of the Society of Jesus." Novices go through various Jesuit experiences, including a 30-day silent retreat, apostolic immersion experiences at various Jesuit ministries throughout the country and the world, and extensive study of the Jesuit constitutions and Ignatian spirituality. Lansing-Reilly Hall was built in 1926-27 as one of the first buildings on the now-University of Detroit Mercy's McNichols campus to serve as the primary residence for the Detroit Jesuit community. Among the advantages for moving the novitiate to Detroit, Daoust cited the Jesuits' presence in Detroit — including at the University of Detroit Mercy, University of Detroit Jesuit High School, Loyola High School, Gesu Parish, SS. Peter and Paul (Jesuit) Parish, the Manresa Retreat Center and the Pope Francis Center and Bridge Housing Facility. "It's a real gift to have all these Jesuit experiences nearby to show the novices what Jesuit ministry is like," Daoust said. Some slight modifications to Lansing-Reilly Hall will be necessary to house up to 30 novices plus staff on a regular basis, including switching from double to single rooms and minor plumbing and electrical updates to the 100-year-old building. The 18 vowed Jesuits currently living at Lansing-Reilly Hall are making arrangements to relocate to other nearby Jesuit residences. Moving the novitiate to Detroit also comes as the Society of Jesus prepares to celebrate its 150th anniversary in the city on July 31, the feast of St. Ignatius of Loyola, with a special Mass celebrated by Cardinal Joseph Tobin of Newark, New Jersey, a Detroit native, and Detroit Archbishop Edward Weisenburger. "I think it's going to make it a much richer experience for the novices in their first two years because it'll be a consistent large community of novices, and even the interchange between the different provinces is going to be enriching, too," Daoust said.

records.title: Defending the fortress (North America)
records.excerpt: Defending the fortress (North America) | Business Council of Canada Skip to main content Follow All Canada's Place in the World Global Affairs North America International Trade All Resources and the Environment Climate Change and Clean Growth Energy Natural Resources All Economic Strategy Jobs and Growth Public Finances Taxation All Industry and Innovation Corporate and Public Governance Digital Economy and Cybersecurity Regulation All Canada's Human Capital Diversity and Inclusion Skills and Talent Entrepreneurship Health and Well-being Immigration Indigenous Relations Reports Analysis Letters Statements Submissions In The News Member Perspectives Opinion Speeches Regulation Stifled by red tape September 5, 2025 Energy Selling to our strengths July 10, 2025 Digital Economy and Cybersecurity Security & Prosperity November 25, 2024 Jobs and Growth Engines of growth September 5, 2024 North America North American energy security May 7, 2025 Member Login Follow Search Follow Search Opinion July 10, 2026 Defending the fortress (North America) by Jack Hughes – Senior Vice President, Planning and Operations, Business Council of Canada Share by Jack Hughes – Senior Vice President, Planning and Operations, Business Council of Canada Canada’s Place in the World Economic Strategy International Trade North America As published in Substack In chess, a ‘fortress’ is an endgame strategy where the player with fewer pieces builds a stable, carefully coordinated, and unbreachable position. Even a player opposite with a material advantage is stymied. The game falls into an endless exchange of stalemated moves which, absent any mistakes, neither player can lose. This may be instructive in assessing Prime Minister Mark Carney’s comments about ‘Fortress North America.’ Carney surprised many when, in an early May speech to the Global Progress Action Summit, he declared: “Canada remains open to deeper integration [with the United States] including options for Fortress North America in selected sectors.” Although he was clear that this was only one option ‘on the table’, and Canada had other alternatives it could pursue, it was the first time he endorsed the idea – at least publicly. While Carney didn’t repeat the term in his prepared remarks three weeks later to the Economic Club of New York, he did so during a fireside chat afterwards: “It’s our strong view, and we’ve been clear about this, a ‘Fortress North America’ in autos, in steel, in aluminum – that’s in everyone’s interest.” This second reference garnered greater interest from trade observers, with some wondering if it signaled a major policy shift. Critics of Fortress North America argue Carney is putting Canadian sovereignty at risk. They warn it could also undermine his goal of doubling non-U.S. exports and attracting billions in foreign investment. Yet there’s another view: Fortress North America is essential to diversifying our global trade and investment partnerships. Carney isn’t trying to enshrine protectionism but preserve Canada’s options and opportunities. On sovereignty, it’s important to recognize ‘Fortress North America’ is not something U.S. President Donald Trump has proposed. In fact, when senior representatives of the Business Council of Canada met with Ambassador Jamieson Greer, the U.S. Trade Representative, he was explicit with us that it’s not a term or concept his president uses personally. He implied Trump’s vision for trade is more focused on ‘Fortress America.’ This isn’t a new problem nor one limited to Republican presidential administrations. In May 2024, two years before Carney offered ‘Fortress North America’ as a solution for economic security, then-Defence Minister Bill Blair applied it to national security under the Biden Administration: “There is a natural tendency for them, quite understandable, that they want to take an approach which is somewhat like a fortress America. My job, our job is to make sure that approach instead is fortress North America.” Blair suggested that to do so, Canada must “demonstrate to our closest ally, our dearest friends and partners, that we are committed to the defence of this continent and both of our countries. We do that through NORAD modernization, we do that for investments in the defence and sovereignty of our own North.” Whether Fortress North America is a Canadian creation, Blair’s blueprint for building it is now being adapted for trade. Reviewing the text of Carney’s twin speeches to the Global Progress Action Summit and the Economic Club of New York, you can see echoes of Blair’s design: He set out to demonstrate to our largest trade and investment partner that Canada is committed to the economic security of this continent and both our countries, through USMCA modernization, investments in defence and the sovereignty of our own economy. Distilled into a Carney soundbite: “Canada Strong will help make America great again.” By specifying the ‘select sectors’ he wanted within the walls of a Fortress North America, Carney was further telegraphing his thinking. Steel, autos, and aluminum imports from Canada to the United States are all subject to section 232 tariffs, ostensibly to safeguard U.S. national security. White House officials have made clear their primary if not only national security metric are U.S. domestic manufacturing capacity utilization rates. Carney has likely put on the table a ‘fortress’ which incentivizes U.S. manufacturing by limiting imports into North America in exchange for 232 tariff relief in those areas and USMCA renewal. The easy targets are dumped or subsidized goods, which can already be subject to countervailing duties under Canadian law. For other imports, there are a variety of tools available, such as harmonizing tariffs or imposing quotas and caps. This take us to a discussion of auto imports from China and the broader question of how can you reconcile more trade with China with advocating for Fortress North America? The answer, in part, was picked up by a ‘hot mic’ at the G7 leaders’ summit when Carney was overheard telling President Trump he put “a cap, we capped, a hard line [on autos]. I thought you’d actually like that” – to which Trump replied, “That’s good. I like that.” The exchange highlights an important dimension of what Trump and Carney are trying to achieve: They both want more trade with China. Fortress North America, then, isn’t a set of rules designed to minimize trade and investment from other countries but, rather, to manage trade and investment with them. Indeed, managed trade and investment is what President Trump went to Beijing to secure with sixteen U.S. CEOs in tow. For Canada, the greatest risk has never been that Trump would ban any and all imports or investment from China into North America but that he’d impose a ‘do-as-I-say-not-as-I-do’ rule where imports and investment from China are welcome in the U.S. but prohibited in Canada and Mexico. A Fortress North America model creates a framework for ideologically consistent, if not necessarily identical, trade regimes for all three. Since the Prime Minister’s own visit to Beijing in January, the Carney government has talked about establishing ‘guardrails’ on Chinese trade and investment. Those guardrails will be the walls of Fortress North America and vice versa. It’s likely no coincidence that Carney delivered his speech to the Economic Club of New York the same day Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi arrived in Ottawa for his first trip to Canada in a decade. Returning to our opening chess analogy, one way to look at the current situation is to envision Prime Minister Carney playing two games at once. Across the board from either the United States or China, the G1 and G2 economies, Canada will always find itself at a material disadvantage. Still, if he can establish a stable, carefully coordinated, mutually-reinforcing ‘fortress’ with both, Carney could position us so that Canada can’t lose. records.title: Federal agency touts operation of cybersecurity sensors across the North
records.excerpt: Title: Federal agency touts operation of cybersecurity sensors across the North URL Source: http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/cse-sensors-north-9.7264185 Published Time: 2026-07-12T10:00:00.000Z Markdown Content: [North](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north) The Communications Security Establishment's latest annual report notes that its Cyber Centre deployed the software on government networks in the Northwest Territories in 2022 followed by Yukon and Nunavut in 2024. ## The deployment to government networks follows a series of high profile incidents ![Image 1](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/a03e3975-d67a-450e-8229-c9ef43519454,1781882045267/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C200%2C200%29%3BResize%3D76) [Niles Niemuth](https://www.cbc.ca/author/niles-niemuth-9.14822) · CBC News · Posted: Jul 12, 2026 6:00 AM EDT | Last Updated: July 12 ![Image 2: Text to Speech Icon](https://www.cbc.ca/a/assets/texttospeech.svg) Listen to this article Estimated 4 minutes The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results. ![Image 3: A sci-fi-looking building.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/d05607ef-1253-48c2-8efb-aa2f3c014cfa,1783622236479/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C254%2C4928%2C2772%29%3B) The Communications Security Establishment Canada (CSEC) complex is pictured in Ottawa in 2013. The agency's Canadian Centre for Cyber Security has rolled out sensors on the IT systems of Northern governments in a bid to prevent cyber attacks.(Sean Kilpatrick/CP) Following a series of high-profile cybersecurity incidents in recent years, a federal agency is now operating tools across the North with the aim of blocking malicious activity by cyber criminals and foreign governments. The Communications Security Establishment (CSE) touts in its latest annual report the operation of digital sensors on territorial government IT systems. The Northwest Territories was the first to have the sensors rolled out on its computer networks in late 2022 followed by the Yukon and Nunavut in 2024. Bridget Walshe with CSE's Canadian Centre for Cyber Security said the sensors are a type of software which can be installed on laptops, servers and in the cloud. The software checks computer systems to see if they are up to date and if there are any vulnerabilities while also scanning for suspicious activity. The information is sent to the centre in Ottawa where it is reviewed by analysts. Any issues are then relayed back to the government agency, which is affected to determine what actions to take. CSE has not released any specific information on the effectiveness of the sensors in countering cyber attacks in the North. However, Walshe said the operations led to 150 “prevention and detection” reports shared with territorial and provincial governments, which account for just five per cent of sensor deployments. The North has seen a number of high-profile incidents in recent years that underscore the need to secure computer networks, including a ransomware virus that [crippled Nunavut government operations](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/nunavut-government-ransomware-attack-1.5347208) in 2019. An [intrusion](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/n-w-t-gov-t-spent-716-000-to-address-cybersecurity-breach-1.6807899) in 2022 cost the government of the Northwest Territories more than $700,000 to contain. The City of Yellowknife took its [services offline](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/city-of-yellowknife-s-network-restored-after-cybersecurity-incident-1.7640359) for a week in 2025 as a precautionary measure in response to a ransomware threat. A wider [breach of cloud software](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/nwt-cyberattack-1.7434164) affected the operations of multiple N.W.T. school boards last year. In March, Prime Minister Mark Carney announced more than $40 billion in investment in the North, with a focus on military infrastructure as well as developing transportation routes that will connect the country. Walshe said growing federal investment is raising interest among those looking to access and manipulate computer networks. “From a cyber security perspective, threat actors are looking at and could use cyber methods to be able to know and get insight and understand that investment in the North to be able to use it to their advantage.” Walshe said the sensors protect users’ privacy and identify suspicious activity without reading emails or documents. However, some have raised concerns over the way in which CSE operates and handles the information it collects. Intelligence Commissioner Simon Noël [highlighted](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/cse-intelligence-commissioner-shared-information-1.7566777) the “improper” sharing of information with international partners between 2020 and 2023 in which data pertaining to Canadians had not been removed. More than a decade ago the British Columbia Civil Liberties Association filed a lawsuit challenging the constitutionality of CSE’s electronic surveillance operations. “There’s a real problem with not recognizing that it's not just the contents of our communications that we have an interest in privacy in but also our physical movements, which can be tracked by metadata, and the fact that we are communicating with others and who we are communicating with, those [people] are also part of metadata," said Aislin Jackson, a lawyer with the civil liberties association. “Metadata can be incredibly revealing and it's not enough to say we respect privacy because we are not touching the content, even if that’s true.” The Northwest Territories Office of the Chief Information Officer referred a request for comment to CSE. A spokesperson for the Yukon government said a variety of vendors and partners help protect government networks, including the cyber centre, but would not say what tools, technologies or systems the government uses. The Nunavut government’s informatics planning and services branch did not respond to a request for comment. ## ABOUT THE AUTHOR ![Image 4](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/a03e3975-d67a-450e-8229-c9ef43519454,1781882045267/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C200%2C200%29%3B) Niles Niemuth has more than a decade of experience in digital news. He has reported and edited stories covering politics, public affairs, labour and community issues in Canada and the United States. He holds a master's degree in history from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee. You can reach him at niles.niemuth@cbc.ca.

The seasonal services will begin in autumn 2026, giving Canadian travellers a new way to reach one of Spain’s most popular Atlantic island destinations without connecting through mainland Europe. Air Travel The new routes represent a significant development for Tenerife [tourism](http://www.travelandtourworld.com/news/article/nkpz6gppvgce/#) and Canada-Spain [travel](http://www.travelandtourworld.com/news/article/nkpz6gppvgce/#) links. By introducing direct services from two major Canadian cities, Air Canada is improving access to the largest Canary Island while supporting leisure travel, tourism growth, and stronger international connectivity. Tenerife has traditionally attracted visitors from Europe due to its year-round climate, volcanic landscapes, beaches, and outdoor experiences. The addition of nonstop Canadian flights opens opportunities to diversify its international visitor markets. ## Air Canada Tenerife Flights Connect Canada Directly With Canary Islands The launch of the **Air Canada Tenerife flights** programme introduces seasonal services from both Toronto and Montreal to Tenerife South Airport. The key developments include: * Air Canada will launch nonstop flights between **Toronto Pearson International Airport and Tenerife South Airport**. * Toronto services will begin on **25 October 2026**. * The route will operate twice weekly on **Thursdays and Sundays**. * Return flights will operate on **Mondays and Fridays**. * A second service will connect **Montreal and Tenerife** from **31 October 2026**. * Montreal flights will operate weekly on **Saturdays**, with return services on Sundays. The new routes provide Canadian travellers with additional options for winter sun holidays, extended vacations, and leisure trips to the Canary Islands. Tenerife is known for its diverse attractions, including volcanic landscapes, coastal resorts, hiking routes, marine activities, and cultural heritage. The island’s year-round mild climate makes it particularly attractive during Canada’s colder months, when travellers often search for warmer destinations. The direct routes could also encourage more Canadians to explore destinations beyond traditional Caribbean and mainland European holiday markets. Advertisement Advertisement ## Air Canada Expands Leisure Network Strategy The Tenerife expansion reflects Air Canada’s wider focus on strengthening leisure travel connections. Airlines have increasingly expanded seasonal international routes as passenger demand shifts toward experience-based holidays and warmer destinations. Leisure routes require careful planning because demand often depends on seasonal travel patterns, tourism trends, and aircraft availability. Air Canada’s decision to add Tenerife services highlights the growing importance of: * Premium leisure travel. * Seasonal international connectivity. * Long-haul vacation markets. * Direct links between secondary tourism destinations and major cities. Toronto and Montreal are among Canada’s largest aviation hubs, allowing Air Canada to connect passengers from across the country through its wider domestic network. ## Tenerife Tourism Gains New North American Opportunity The new flights are expected to support Tenerife’s tourism industry by improving access from an important long-haul market. Air Travel Canada represents an attractive source market due to: Advertisement Advertisement * Strong outbound travel demand. * Interest in warm-weather destinations. * Growing demand for unique European experiences. * High-value tourism spending potential. Improved connectivity can benefit: * Hotels and resorts. * Restaurants and attractions. * Local transport providers. * Tour operators. * Experience-based tourism businesses. For island destinations, aviation capacity is one of the most important factors influencing visitor growth. Unlike mainland destinations with rail and road alternatives, islands depend heavily on reliable air links. ## Impact on Canary Islands Air Connectivity The Air Canada routes represent a broader trend of expanding long-haul access to the Canary Islands. Historically, most international visitors to Tenerife have arrived from European markets, particularly the United Kingdom, Germany, and mainland Spain. New North American connections help strengthen the island’s global tourism profile. Direct flights can also support greater awareness of Tenerife among travellers who may not previously have considered the Canary Islands due to limited accessibility. The new routes may encourage other airlines and [tourism](http://www.travelandtourworld.com/news/article/nkpz6gppvgce/#) stakeholders to explore additional opportunities between North America and Atlantic island destinations. As these are seasonal leisure services, schedules may vary depending on demand and operational planning. Travellers should also consider booking accommodation and activities early during peak winter [travel](http://www.travelandtourworld.com/news/article/nkpz6gppvgce/#) periods, as Tenerife remains a popular destination throughout the year. ## Future Outlook for Canada Canary Islands Travel The launch of Air Canada’s Tenerife flights highlights the continued recovery and evolution of global leisure aviation. As travellers seek more direct routes and unique destinations, airlines are expected to continue developing services that connect major outbound markets with attractive holiday locations. The success of the Toronto and Montreal routes could influence future frequency increases or additional North American connections to the Canary Islands. records.title: [ED] SK hynix's triumphant Nasdaq debut
records.excerpt: SK hynix has achieved a milestone that extends far beyond the fortunes of a single company. By raising approximately $26.5 billion through its offe... Employees of semiconductor and memory chip maker SK hynix take part in the company’s opening bell ceremony at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York City, July 10, marking its initial public offering (IPO). (Reuters/Angelina Katsanis) SK hynix has achieved a milestone that extends far beyond the fortunes of a single company. By raising approximately $26.5 billion through its offering of American depositary receipts (ADRs) on Nasdaq, the semiconductor giant has completed the largest capital raising ever by a foreign company in the U.S. market. Even more remarkable was the pricing: The ADRs were offered at a premium to the closing price of the company's shares in Seoul, overturning the long-standing convention that large equity offerings require a discount to attract investors. The transaction is more than a financial success. It represents a powerful endorsement by global investors of SK hynix's leadership in the artificial intelligence (AI) era. Far from viewing the company as merely another memory chip manufacturer, the market has recognized it as a strategic technology leader whose future is closely tied to the explosive growth of AI. In securing a premium valuation from the world's deepest capital market, SK hynix has demonstrated that Korean tech companies can compete not only in manufacturing but also in earning the confidence of global investors. The significance of this transaction becomes even clearer in light of the changing nature of competition in the semiconductor industry. The race for AI dominance is no longer determined solely by technological innovation. It has become equally a contest of capital. The companies capable of mobilizing enormous financial resources most quickly will be best positioned to expand production, accelerate research and development and secure long-term technological leadership. SK hynix's newly raised funds will help finance large-scale investments, including semiconductor fabrication facilities in Yongin, Gyeonggi Province, and advanced packaging operations in Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province, while reinforcing its leadership in high-bandwidth memory, a critical component for AI computing. The scale of such investment is staggering, yet it has become unavoidable. The day before SK hynix's ADR listing, Micron Technology announced plans to invest more than $250 billion in the United States by 2035. The message is unmistakable: In today's semiconductor industry, access to capital has become as strategically important as engineering excellence. For Korea, the benefits of SK hynix's success extend well beyond one company's balance sheet. A substantial inflow of dollar-denominated capital can support investment, create jobs, strengthen exports and contribute to greater exchange-rate stability. More importantly, sustained investment in AI and semiconductor manufacturing could further establish Korea as a global hub for advanced technologies, attracting additional foreign direct investment and increasing international interest in other innovative Korean firms. If managed well, this momentum could even help narrow the persistent "Korea discount" that has long depressed valuations in the domestic equity market. Yet this extraordinary achievement also exposes an uncomfortable reality. That one of Korea's premier corporations chose New York rather than Seoul for such a landmark capital raising reflects the limitations of Korea's own financial markets. If companies increasingly conclude that they must turn abroad to receive fair valuations and raise growth capital efficiently, more leading enterprises may follow the same path. Such a trend would inevitably weaken the domestic market through declining liquidity, reduced investor participation and the offshoring of both capital and influence. The issue extends beyond a single listing. It raises a fundamental question about whether Korea's capital markets are adequately equipped to support globally competitive companies through their next stage of growth. Despite possessing world-class manufacturers, Korea continues to rely on foreign financial centers to provide the scale of funding and international investor base that its leading firms require. In the process, financial activity — including underwriting fees and related services — is captured abroad rather than by Korea's own financial industry. Addressing this challenge demands more than symbolic reform. Policymakers should accelerate efforts to improve corporate governance, strengthen market transparency, streamline regulations and enhance access for international investors. Equally important is the creation of a policy environment that encourages long-term investment rather than discouraging companies from raising fresh capital for future growth. Excessive emphasis on short-term shareholder returns at the expense of strategic investment risks undermining the very competitiveness that investors seek. The government must also look beyond today's semiconductor champions. Korea's next generation of globally competitive industries will require the same combination of innovation, patient capital and policy support that enabled the country's rise as a semiconductor powerhouse. Cultivating these future growth engines will ultimately determine whether Korea can sustain its technological leadership in an increasingly competitive global economy. SK hynix's Nasdaq debut deserves celebration as a landmark achievement for Korea's industry. But its greatest significance lies in the challenge it presents. The transaction has shown that Korea possesses companies capable of commanding global confidence. The task now is to build a domestic capital market equally worthy of that confidence. Only then can Korea move beyond overcoming the "Korea discount" and begin to earn a genuine "Korea premium."

records.title: SK hynix enters Nasdaq ADR listing ...Pushes full-scale push into U.S. capital markets
records.excerpt: Building on AI memory competitiveness to expand its base of global investors Holding an opening bell ceremony and starting official trading…Strengthens its position as a key partner for AI Building on AI memory competitiveness to expand its base of global investors Holding an opening bell ceremony and starting official trading…Strengthens its position as a key partner for AI At around 10 a.m. on the 10th (local time), at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, the chairman of SK Group, Chey Tae-won, SK hynix CEO Kwak No-jung, and Ko Seung-beom, SK hynix outside director and chair of the board of directors, ring the bell to announce the start of Nasdaq ADR trading. Photo=SK hynix SK hynix has entered the Nasdaq (NASDAQ) market in the United States by listing its ADR (American Depositary Receipt). Leveraging its competitive edge in the AI memory market, the company is expanding its base of global investors and launching a full-scale drive to tap U.S. capital markets. According to SK hynix (CEO and President Kwak No-jung) on the 11th, the company held an ADR listing commemoration 'Opening Bell' event at the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square, New York, on the 10th (U.S. time) and began official trading. A host of key executives from the group and the company attended the event, including Chey Tae-won, chairman of SK Group, Chey Jae-won, senior vice chairman of SK Group, and Kwak No-jung, CEO of SK hynix. Kwak No-jung, SK hynix CEO, gives a presentation on its AI memory vision at the Nasdaq 'Opening Bell' event. Photo=SK hynix With this listing as a starting point, SK hynix plans to expand its base of global investors in U.S. capital markets and strengthen its position as a key partner for AI. Before the listing, it held a roadshow targeting global institutional investors in major regions including the United States, Europe, and Asia, and the company said investors showed high interest in the company's technology and growth prospects as it leads the AI memory market. As the AI market expands and data center investment increases, demand for AI memory is also rising rapidly. SK hynix secures competitiveness in the related market by supplying AI memory products such as high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to global big tech companies. The company expects this ADR listing will be more than a simple means of raising funds, serving as an opportunity to improve global investors' accessibility and to expand cooperation with next-generation computing ecosystems. Based on that, it plans to discover new business opportunities and strengthen strategic partnerships, while also contributing to the development of the AI industry ecosystem. Chey Tae-won, chairman of SK Group, Kwak No-jung, SK hynix CEO, and other key executives pose for a commemorative photo in front of the MarketSite. (From the eighth in the first row on the left: Chey Jae-won, senior vice chairman of SK Square; Kwak No-jung, SK hynix CEO; Chey Tae-won, chairman of SK Group; Ko Seung-beom, SK hynix outside director and chair of the board of directors; Yoo Jeong-jun, vice chairman in charge of the Americas at SK (Inc.). Photo=SK hynix In his congratulatory remarks, CEO Kwak No-jung said, "Based on trust, innovation, and growth, we will further strengthen our leadership in AI memory technology," and added, "Through innovation, we will broaden the possibilities of memory and grow together with customers everywhere there is AI." Meanwhile, for SK hynix's ADR, which successfully started its first trade today, the deposit payment for the offering will be completed on the 14th in U.S. time. The newly issued common shares (new shares) that underpin this ADR are expected to be additionally listed on or around the 29th (Korea time) on the Korea Exchange's securities market. #SK hynix #AI memory #opening bell #AI key partner #United States #capital markets #Nasdaq #AI memory market #Park Yong-jun #Kwak No-jung CEO Chey Tae-won #ADR #American depositary receipt #opening bell #market site #New York #Times Square #Chairman Chey Tae-won #SK Group #Chey Jae-won senior vice chairman #institutional investors 박용준 sasori0624@theggnews.com

records.title: Sin Lian Seng, Fasteners Supplier and Solar EPC Provider, Files for Nasdaq Capital Market IPO
records.excerpt: Sin Lian Seng Construction, a Singapore-based fastener distributor and commercial & industrial solar EPC provider, filed for an initial public offering on the Nasdaq Capital Market. The company plans to list under the ticker “ININ” and offer 6,250,000 ordinary shares at an expected price range of… Sin Lian Seng, Fasteners Supplier and Solar EPC Provider, Files for Nasdaq Capital Market IPO 3 min read Sin Lian Seng Construction, a Singapore-based fastener distributor and commercial & industrial solar EPC provider, filed for an initial public offering on the Nasdaq Capital Market. The company plans to list under the ticker “ININ” and offer 6,250,000 ordinary shares at an expected price range of $4.00 to $5.00 per share. Prior to this offering, there has been no public market for the company’s shares. Business Description Sin Lian Seng is a Singapore-based supplier of industrial fasteners and a turnkey solar engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) provider focused on commercial and industrial (C&I) projects. Through Sin Lian Seng Bolts & Nuts Pte Ltd, founded in 1986, the company supplies bolts, nuts, washers, U-bolts and related components to construction, mechanical & electrical, marine and manufacturing customers. It maintains ISO 9001:2015 quality systems and works with a network of manufacturers, including FPC-certified suppliers, to meet local standards and project needs. Following the 2025 acquisition of Lumenx Energy Pte. Ltd., the company added distributed solar EPC services spanning system design, equipment sourcing, installation, grid connection, and commissioning. The solar business targets C&I rooftops in Singapore and intends to expand into Southeast Asia and the United States. Revenue comes primarily from fastener sales, complemented by project-based solar EPC contracts. Competitive strengths include a long operating history, diversified product and service offerings, established customer and supplier relationships, and quality accreditation. Market Overview Total addressable market : Global industrial fasteners market projected to reach about US$125.22 billion by 2029, per industry research. Market growth : Global fasteners market expected to grow at roughly 6.1% CAGR through 2029; Singapore construction industry forecast to expand ~4.1% in 2025. Market position : Long-operating Singapore supplier with ISO 9001:2015 accreditation and relationships with FPC-certified manufacturers. Key competitors : Local and regional fastener distributors and multinational EPC providers and utilities in solar. Industry trends : Infrastructure spending in Singapore (public housing, MRT expansion) and rising corporate sustainability targets drive fastener demand and solar EPC adoption; Singapore targets at least 2 GWp of solar by 2030. Operational Metrics Customers : Major Singapore contractors across construction, M&E, marine, and manufacturing; growing C&I solar client base. Locations : Principal executive office and warehouse at 30 Kranji Loop, #02-12, Singapore; facility approx. 1,418 sqm. Geographic presence : Core operations in Singapore with planned EPC expansion into the U.S. and Southeast Asia. Partnerships : Multi-sourced manufacturer network (including FPC-certified suppliers) and ISO 9001:2015 accreditation by BSI. Other key metrics : FY2025 revenue mix – fasteners S$6.31 million; solar EPC S$0.75 million. Financials Highlights Revenue (current) : S$7.07 million (US$5.50 million) for FY2025 Revenue growth : Up ~29% year over year (from S$5.51 million in FY2024) Gross profit : S$2.19 million (US$1.70 million) (~31% margin) Operating income : S$1.02 million for FY2025 Net income : S$1.25 million (US$0.97 million) for FY2025 Management Sam Zheng Sun , Chairman and Chief Executive Officer - Over 20 years in private equity and corporate management; former roles at Affinity Equity Partners, Sequoia Capital; MBA, UCLA Anderson. Guohao Chen , Chief Financial Officer - 10+ years in investment and capital markets; prior roles at Haitong Securities and Minmetals Innovative Investment; Master’s, Renmin University. Kewei Soh , Chief Operating Officer and Director - 15+ years in energy, real estate, industrial sectors; experience in business development and operations; B.Eng. (NTU) and M.S. Finance. Gan Ker Wei , Independent Director - 20+ years in equity capital markets; prior roles at JPMorgan, Deutsche Bank, Sun Hung Kai. Tang Poon Tung Denny , Independent Director Nominee - Senior finance executive; CFO at Scienjoy Holding Corporation; prior leadership roles across media and internet companies. George S. Geh , Independent Director Nominee - 30+ years in PE, consulting and corporate; former MD at Lone Star Funds and AlixPartners; ex-McKinsey. IPO Structure Issuer : Sin Lian Seng Construction Filing date : July 10, 2026 Proposed ticker : ININ Exchange : Nasdaq Capital Market Price range : $4.00–$5.00 per share Offering size : Approximately $25.0–$31.3 million (gross), before any over-allotment Shares offered : 6,250,000 shares (plus 937,500 over-allotment option) Lead underwriters : Kingswood Capital Partners, LLC (representative) Use of proceeds : ~40% to expand EPC business (including U.S. and Southeast Asia), ~35% for fasteners supply expansion and logistics upgrades, ~15% for strategic acquisitions and investments, and the balance for working capital and general corporate purposes. Original SEC Filing: Sin Lian Seng Construction - F-1 - Jul. 10, 2026 Disclaimer This is an AI-powered summary. It may contain inaccuracies. Consider verifying important information with the source. records.title: SK Hynix begins first trading on U.S. Nasdaq
records.excerpt: SK Hynix has entered overseas capital markets directly, beginning official trading on the U.S. Nasdaq through a listing of American depositary receipts, the company said. It held an opening bell event at Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square, New York. Executives including SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won attended. The company said it plans to broaden its U.S. investor base and strengthen its position as a key AI partner. SK Hynix has entered overseas capital markets directly. SK Hynix said on the 10th (U.S. time) it began official trading on the U.S. Nasdaq market through a listing of ADRs, certificates issued based on foreign company shares held by a depositary institution. The company held a commemorative opening bell event at Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square, New York, on the day.The event was attended by key group and company executives, including SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won (최태원), Vice Chairman Chey Jae-won (최재원) and SK Hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung (곽노정). SK Hynix has secured a competitive edge in high bandwidth memory, or HBM, a high-performance memory made by stacking multiple layers to increase data processing speed. This memory quickly processes data needed for AI computing and determines the performance of AI accelerators.As data centres spread rapidly in the era of artificial intelligence and demand for such memory rises sharply, SK Hynix said it plans to use the listing to broaden its investor base in the U.S. capital market and strengthen its position as a key AI partner. The company said it held roadshows for institutional investors in major regions including the United States, Europe and Asia ahead of the listing, and investors focused on its competitiveness and growth potential in leading the AI memory market.In a congratulatory speech, Kwak stressed trust, innovation and growth. "I thank the investors and customers who believed in us. We will expand the boundaries of what memory can do through innovation, and support our employees so they can achieve even greater accomplishments," he said. "SK Hynix will prove its technology leadership and be present wherever there is AI," he said.SK Hynix's listing is expected to be a step to strengthen connections with the next-generation computing ecosystem beyond raising funds. Payment of the offering proceeds for SK Hynix's ADRs, which began first trading on the day, will be completed on the 14th (U.S. time). New common shares that underpin the ADRs are expected to be additionally listed on the Korea Exchange's main board around the 29th.

RY stock, issued by Royal Bank of Canada (ISIN CA7800871021), represents an ownership stake in one of North America’s largest diversified financial institutions with a long history of stable earnings and dividend payments. For US retail investors, the shares trade actively on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the ticker RY and are also accessible via the bank’s presence in US capital markets, making the name a familiar part of the broader North American financial landscape. The company’s scale, diversified business mix, and longstanding profitability profile mean that RY stock is often regarded as a proxy for the health of the Canadian banking sector and a structural play on household, corporate, and capital markets activity across Canada and select international geographies. Royal Bank of Canada’s business foundation Royal Bank of Canada operates as a full-service financial institution offering retail banking, commercial banking, wealth management, insurance, and capital markets services to individual and institutional clients. The bank’s retail franchise provides checking and savings accounts, credit cards, personal loans, residential mortgages, and small-business services to millions of customers, underpinning a recurring revenue base driven by interest margins and fee income. Commercial and corporate banking adds lending, cash management, trade finance, and advisory services for larger businesses, supporting the bank’s role in financing economic activity across sectors such as real estate, energy, manufacturing, and services. Beyond traditional banking, Royal Bank of Canada has built a sizable wealth management platform serving affluent and high-net-worth clients with investment advisory, portfolio management, and trust services. Insurance offerings, including life, health, and property coverage, add another source of diversified fees and premiums. The bank’s capital markets division contributes trading, underwriting, and advisory revenues across equity, fixed income, foreign exchange, and derivatives markets, connecting the institution to global investors, corporations, and governments. Together, these operating segments give RY stock an earnings profile that is not tied to a single product or geography, which can help smooth performance across different phases of the interest rate and credit cycles. Net interest income reflects the spread between interest earned on loans and securities and interest paid on deposits and wholesale funding; it tends to rise when benchmark interest rates increase and the bank can reprice assets faster than liabilities, but it can compress when competitive pressures force more generous deposit rates or when loan growth slows. Fee income arises from services such as card processing, account maintenance, wealth management, and insurance, giving the bank revenue streams that are less sensitive to interest rates and more tied to client activity and asset levels. Credit quality is another central factor for RY stock because loan loss provisions directly affect earnings and signal how management views risk in the portfolio. In periods of economic strength, defaults and delinquencies tend to be low, which supports modest provisioning and higher net income. When macro conditions weaken or specific sectors experience stress, provisions can increase as the bank recognizes potential credit losses, which weighs on reported profits. Operating efficiency, often assessed via ratios comparing expenses to revenue, reflects how well the bank controls costs while growing its franchise. A sustained focus on technology, process optimization, and branch network management can improve efficiency, supporting profitability even when revenue growth is moderate. Structural differences between Canadian and US regulatory frameworks, capital requirements, and housing markets mean that Royal Bank of Canada’s risk profile can differ from that of large US peers, especially in areas such as mortgage exposures and consumer lending. Over long horizons, Canadian banks have generally emphasized conservative underwriting and strong capital positions, which many investors see as supportive of dividend sustainability and resilience during downturns. This backdrop leads some market participants to view RY stock as a long-term core holding for financial-sector exposure rather than a purely cyclical trade. Regulation, capital, and dividends The regulatory environment and capital position play a crucial role in shaping the investment case for RY stock. As a systemically important bank in Canada, Royal Bank of Canada is subject to stringent capital and liquidity requirements designed to ensure resilience in the face of economic stress or market volatility. These requirements influence how much capital the bank must hold against various assets and off-balance-sheet exposures, which in turn impacts its leverage, return on equity, and capacity to distribute earnings through dividends and share repurchases. A robust capital buffer provides flexibility to absorb losses, support lending growth, and maintain payouts, but it also imposes constraints that the bank must manage carefully. Dividend policy is particularly important to investors who focus on RY stock as an income-generating asset. Royal Bank of Canada has a long record of paying regular dividends, and the bank’s management typically aims to align dividend growth with sustainable earnings expansion while staying within regulatory capital guidelines. For many income-focused investors, the reliability and trajectory of dividends are as significant as near-term share price movements, especially in a sector where payout cuts during crises can be highly visible. The fintech giant reported robust preliminary FY2026 results, including $243 billion in cross-border volume and $1.9 billion in transaction revenue, underscoring its disruptive potential against traditional banks. Despite impressive growth and a transparent, low-cost model, Wise faces significant regulatory hurdles and intense competition in the U.S., which could impact its profitability and long-term market penetration. What's Driving Wise Group's Nasdaq Debut and Investor Interest? Wise Group PLC, the global technology company renowned for its low-cost cross-border payments, officially shifted its primary listing to Nasdaq on May 11, 2026 , while maintaining a secondary listing in London. This strategic move is a clear declaration of intent: Wise is targeting the U.S. as its biggest market opportunity, aiming to tap into the world's deepest and most liquid capital markets. CEO Kristo Käärmann highlighted the immense potential, noting that $43 trillion moves across borders globally each year, with Americans alone projected to lose $43 billion in hidden cross-border fees in 2026. The company's preliminary financial year 2026 results, released ahead of the Nasdaq debut, provide a compelling backdrop for this ambition. Wise facilitated a staggering $243 billion in cross-border volume, marking a 31% year-over-year increase. Transaction revenue climbed to $1.9 billion , up 22% year-over-year, driven by $1.3 billion from cross-border transactions and $0.6 billion from card and other services. Customer holdings also surged 40% to $39 billion , including $9 billion in Wise Assets. These numbers reflect strong, sustained demand for modern fintech solutions that offer speed, cost-effectiveness, and transparency, directly challenging the legacy banking system. This dual listing strategy is designed to boost Wise's visibility among institutional investors and accelerate its global expansion, particularly within the U.S. The company's CFO, Emmanuel Thomassin, emphasized the "massive opportunity" in the U.S. banking sector, where Wise's technology and infrastructure offer a distinct advantage over existing options. The move also signals a structural tilt away from London's historically lower valuations for growth fintechs, seeking a more favorable environment for capital raising and investor engagement. Can Wise Truly Disrupt the U.S. Banking Sector? Wise's ambition to disrupt the U.S. banking sector is rooted in its core value proposition: transparent, low-cost, and fast cross-border payments. Traditional banks often charge $10-$35 for sending transfers, apply hidden exchange rate markups of 2-4% , and incur intermediary bank fees, leading to total costs often ranging from 8-12% of a $1,000 transfer. In contrast, Wise typically charges 0.5-1.5% for the same transfer, using the mid-market exchange rate without hidden markups. This cost efficiency, combined with speed— 60% of Wise transfers arrived instantly in Q1 2024, and 95% within 24 hours—presents a formidable challenge to incumbents. The company's strategy extends beyond just offering a better service; it involves building direct infrastructure. Wise applied in July 2025 to create a national trust bank in the U.S. under the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) and plans to seek a master account with the Federal Reserve. If granted, these approvals would allow Wise to bypass intermediary banks, settle U.S. dollar payments directly with the Fed, cut costs, speed up transfers, and gain tighter control over its largest currency flow. This direct connection is crucial for its "network based on direct connection to the payment systems" vision. However, the path to disruption is fraught with challenges. The U.S. banking industry is undergoing significant structural transformation, marked by accelerating mergers and acquisitions and intense regulatory scrutiny. Incumbent lenders are fiercely protective of their market share, voicing concerns over fintech disruptors gaining full banking privileges. Wise itself faced a $4.2 million AML penalty from state financial regulators in July 2025 for deficiencies in its anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing controls, highlighting the complex and fragmented U.S. regulatory environment. This penalty has led to a "mathematical over-correction" in its automated compliance, sometimes resulting in aggressive account freezes. What Are Wise Group's Key Growth Prospects in Cross-Border Payments? Wise Group PLC's growth prospects in the cross-border payments market remain robust, driven by several macro trends and its differentiated business model. The global cross-border payments market is expanding rapidly, fueled by increasing international trade, e-commerce, and remittances. PYMNTS Intelligence research found that 14% of American consumers made a cross-border payment in the prior 12 months , with nearly two-thirds using digital wallets. This shift towards digital-first solutions plays directly into Wise's strengths. The company's ability to offer transparent, low-cost, and fast transfers positions it favorably against traditional banks. Wise processed £49.4 billion in cross-border transaction volume in Q4 ending March 2026, a 26% year-over-year jump, serving 11.3 million active customers, up 22% . This momentum indicates strong customer acquisition and retention, as users increasingly adopt Wise not just for one-off transfers but as their primary multi-currency account. The "OwnWise" program, offering customer loyalty benefits for shareholders, further aims to deepen this engagement. Beyond individual consumers, Wise is also expanding its reach into the business sector. Its Wise Business account offers competitive fees, especially for transfers under $50,000 , where it often outperforms institutional hybrid solutions. The company's API infrastructure is also a significant growth driver, enabling businesses to integrate Wise's payment capabilities directly into their operations. This allows for real-time auditability and compliance transparency, appealing to SMEs and enterprises looking to optimize their international payment infrastructure for scale and compliance. However, competition is intensifying. Juniper Research identifies numerous players in the cross-border payments landscape, from infrastructure providers like Mastercard and Visa to money transfer services like PayPal, Remitly, and Revolut. While Wise excels in bank-to-bank transfers with its mid-market rates, competitors like Remitly might have an edge in emerging markets or cash pickup destinations. For very large transfers (over $50,000 ), currency brokers like OFX or institutional desks can offer more competitive rates and personalized service, suggesting Wise's sweet spot might be in the mid-range transaction volumes. What Regulatory and Competitive Headwinds Does Wise Face? Wise's ambitious U.S. expansion is not without significant regulatory and competitive headwinds that could temper its growth trajectory and profitability. The U.S. regulatory landscape for money transmitters is notoriously complex, with oversight at both state and federal levels. The $4.2 million AML penalty in July 2025 served as a stark reminder of the stringent compliance requirements, particularly concerning customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, and suspicious activity reporting (SAR). records.title: SK Hynix's Record $26.5 Billion Nasdaq Debut Sparks New Wave of Foreign Listings, Nasdaq's Griggs Says
records.excerpt: SK Hynix's record Nasdaq debut raises $26.5 billion, sparking interest from global firms in U.S. listings. The move highlights the growing appeal of American capital markets for international... South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix's record-breaking Wall Street debut is fueling a fresh surge of interest from international companies eyeing U.S. exchanges, according to Nasdaq Inc. leadership, as the memory-chip giant's historic listing reshapes expectations for how foreign firms tap American capital markets.SK Hynix began trading on the Nasdaq Friday under the temporary ticker SKHYV after pricing its American depositary receipts at $149 apiece, raising $26.5 billion in the largest-ever U.S. share sale by a non-American company. The offering topped Alibaba's $25 billion raise in 2014 and ranks as the third-largest U.S. listing on record, trailing only SpaceX's $85.7 billion debut last month and Saudi Aramco's $29.4 billion offering in 2019.The stock surged in its opening session, jumping as much as 17% to around $174.50 shortly after trading opened, following earlier indications the shares could trade as much as 21% above their offering price. The company sold 177.9 million ADRs, with the securities structured so U.S. investors can buy in at roughly a tenth of the cost of a full share on SK Hynix's primary Seoul listing. Demand for the offering was strong: investors sought more than seven times the number of shares available before the deal was priced, according to Reuters.Nasdaq Inc. President Nelson Griggs said the blockbuster listing is already spurring other international companies to weigh the U.S. market for either new initial public offerings or ADR sales, Bloomberg reported. Griggs made the remarks Friday, fresh off a trip to Europe during which he met with executives considering crossing the Atlantic for capital. According to Bloomberg, Griggs grouped the foreign issuers showing interest in U.S. listings into two categories: early-stage companies that haven't yet listed anywhere, and established firms with existing local listings that are weighing the addition of U.S. ADRs.The enthusiasm reflects a broader pattern that has defined 2026's IPO market, in which international companies riding the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom have looked to U.S. exchanges for deeper capital pools and stronger valuations than they can typically command at home. Analysts have pointed to a persistent valuation gap between SK Hynix and its American rival, Micron Technology, as one motivation behind the Nasdaq listing. At the time of its debut, SK Hynix traded at roughly 5.5 times forward earnings, compared with Micron's 6.66 times, a discrepancy the company has said it hopes the U.S. listing will help close.SK Hynix Chairman Chey Tae-won traveled to New York personally for the company's bell-ringing ceremony, underscoring how central the listing is to the conglomerate's broader ambitions. "It's a kind of dream, and now it's a dream come true," Chey told CNBC's Kristina Partsinevelos on Friday. Chey said that when he meets with customers and partners, demand for chips consistently outpaces expectations, telling CNBC that even after SK Hynix announced plans to double its production capacity within five years, customers pushed back that the increase wouldn't be enough.The listing arrives amid an extraordinary run of financial performance for the company. SK Hynix posted first-quarter revenue of 52.58 trillion won, or about $38.1 billion, a 198% jump from the same period a year earlier, with net profit margin climbing to 77% from 46%, driven largely by high-bandwidth memory chips critical to AI accelerators. Analysts polled by data provider LSEG expect SK Hynix's revenue to more than triple again this year to roughly $235 billion.SK Hynix's market value stood at about $1 trillion as of Friday, making it South Korea's second-largest company behind Samsung Electronics. Its Seoul-listed shares have climbed 222% so far this year and roughly 634% over the past twelve months, a rally tied to the artificial intelligence industry's voracious appetite for the high-bandwidth memory that powers AI chips from Nvidia and other producers. SK Hynix controls roughly 58% of the global HBM market, according to Counterpoint Research figures cited by CNBC, ahead of competitors Micron and Samsung, which each hold about 21%.Market strategists framed the debut as a significant test of investor conviction in the durability of the broader AI trade, particularly after a recent pullback in semiconductor stocks tied to concerns over slowing AI spending. "Global semiconductors is the most crowded trade in the world right now," Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital in New York, said. Giuseppe Sette, co-founder of investment analysis platform Reflexivity, said the Nasdaq listing was a deliberate strategic choice by the company. "This is the purest large-cap way for U.S. investors to own the AI-memory theme, and Hynix deliberately picked Nasdaq to tap that demand and the higher valuations U.S. chip names command versus Seoul," Sette said, adding that "SK Hynix gets its deal done on the strength of the story, but companies coming after it may face a tougher, more selective market."The offering also drew attention from U.S. policymakers. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick visited a Micron event this week and said he was already in discussions with Samsung and SK Hynix about building additional manufacturing facilities in the United States, seeking to prevent South Korea from continuing to dominate advanced chip production. Micron has separately committed to investing $250 billion in new U.S. manufacturing, a pledge the company says will create more than 90,000 jobs.SK Hynix has said proceeds from the U.S. offering will help fund new production facilities and equipment purchases, including advanced lithography machines, with the bulk of its expansion still concentrated in South Korea. The company has also committed to a $4 billion advanced packaging plant in Indiana as part of a broader push to establish a domestic U.S. manufacturing footprint alongside its listing.Regular trading in SK Hynix shares under the permanent ticker SKHY is set to begin Monday. For Nasdaq, the listing represents a marquee win in its ongoing competition with rival exchanges for high-profile international offerings, and Griggs' comments suggest the exchange sees the SK Hynix deal as a template it hopes to replicate with other large overseas issuers in the months ahead.

B.LEAGUE B.LEAGUE B.革新とは 審査基準・結果 参入決定クラブ 選手契約・ドラフト サラリーキャップ制度 ロスター・オンザコート 選手登録制度 ドラフト制度 シーズンの変更点 レギュラーシーズン ポストシーズン よくある質問 B.革新 | B.Innovation | 2026 TIP OFF 5分でわかる B.革新 B.LEAGUEはどう変わる？ 審査基準・結果 のページを更新しました。 2025.11.19[WED] B.LEAGUE ONE / B.LEAGUE NEXTの参入クラブ を公開しました。 2025.10.30[THU] ドラフト制度 のページを更新しました。 2025.3.12[WED] 全てのニュースを見る B.INNOVATION 世界一型破りな ライブスポーツエンタメを目指し B.LEAGUEが変わります 2016年にB.LEAGUEが開幕して以来、リーグとクラブの事業規模は大きく成長しました。 しかし、B.LEAGUEが「バスケで日本を元気に」を実現するため、また、クラブがステークホルダーや地域の皆さまを幸せにできる存在となるためには、クラブが今以上に経営力をつけ、長期的視野で成長のための投資を行うことができる環境を作ることが不可欠です。 そこで、B.LEAGUEは、「強化」「経営」「社会性」の3つの軸に沿って、2026年からリーグ構造の変更を伴う、大きな変革を行います。 B.革新とは OVERVIEW 5分でわかる「B.革新」 B.LEAGUEはどう変わる？ 2026-27シーズンから新たなリーグ構造に生まれ変わります。 2026-27シーズンから新たなリーグ構造となり、競技成績に基づいた昇格・降格が廃止されます。 各ディビジョンに参入するためには厳正なる審査をクリアしなければなりません。 審査には「平均入場者数」「売上高」「ホームアリーナ」等の条件が設けられており、2026-27シーズンに向けて続々と参入クラブが決定しています。 CRITERIA 審査 クラブ・アリーナを軸に地域が発展するための審査基準を設定。財務健全性や経営基盤の安定性を審査基準として強化。クラブごとに運営指針の達成度や将来ビジョンを審査し透明性を確保。B.LEAGUE PREMIERだけではなく、B.LEAGUE ONE、B.LEAGUE NEXTの審査基準を引き上げ。 審査 CLUBS 参入クラブ 参入決定のクラブ一覧。リーグの発展と地域バスケの拡大を目指す。新規参入後の戦力均衡を図り、長期的な競争力を確保。地域振興やファンコミュニティ形成に積極的な取り組みを推奨。 参入クラブ SCHEDULE B.LEAGUE PREMIERでは、これまでのB.LEAGUEのレギュラーシーズンの形式から大きく変わり、ポストシーズンについてもFINALSがHOME/AWAY方式になるなど、大きな変更点が設けられていきます。 レギュラーシーズン B.LEAGUE PREMIERは露出拡大・アリーナ運営・選手コンディション・AWAY観戦のしやすさを鑑み、週末試合と平日試合をバランスよく開催。B.LEAGUE ONE、B.LEAGUE NEXTは現在のB1、B2と同様の形式を採用予定。 レギュラーシーズン ポストシーズン B.LEAGUE PREMIERは現在中央開催されているFINALSを出場クラブのホーム＆アウェーでの開催に変更。 試合数も3戦先勝方式(最大5試合)に変更されます。B.LEAGUE ONEは「広さ」の全国リーグとしてより多くの地区代表クラブが優勝争いを行うことでリーグ全体の盛り上げを狙い、ポストシーズンへの進出クラブ数を16クラブへ拡大。 ポストシーズン PLAYER SYSTEM 新しいB.LEAGUEには、これまでに無かったたくさんの制度が設けられ、よりクラブ同士の実力が均衡するような仕組みが採用されます。 サラリーキャップ制度 クラブ間の財政バランスを保ち、リーグの競争力維持が目的。選手の報酬上限と下限を設け、クラブの健全な財政を推進。最低年俸制度により、安定した選手生活を支援。 サラリーキャップ制度 ロスター・オンザコート 試合出場や登録可能枠の調整で、競技力の強化を目指す。外国籍選手は登録3名、出場はB.PREMIERでオンザコートフリーを実現。帰化/アジア特別枠の出場機会は継続維持しつつも、U22枠やユース育成特別枠といったユース選手、ユース出身選手の活躍機会を拡大。 ロスター・オンザコート 選手登録制度 選手流動性制度の再設計として、B.LEAGUE PREMIER内の移籍を柔軟に行えるルールを導入。また、クラブの意思で当該選手を期限付き移籍させることが可能な「育成契約選手制度」を設けます。 選手登録制度 ドラフト制度 未来のスター選手発掘に向けたドラフト制度を新設。クラブが公平に新人選手を獲得できる仕組みを確立し、指名順位や契約期間、報酬基準についてのルールをまとめました。 ドラフト制度 TOP B.革新とは 審査基準・結果 参入決定クラブ
